Broker Development Manager
raw.description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

THE ROLE 

Our brokers play a crucial role in making this a reality. We’re an AI-first business, so whatever the role, we want people who reach for AI by default, stay curious about what it can do, and use it to work faster and think bigger. You’ll use AI day to day, from researching brokers to preparing for meetings, so more of your time goes on the conversations that win business. We’re looking for an ambitious and passionate Broker Development Manager to accelerate our distribution through brokers. In this role, you’ll maximise existing broker relationships and build strong, strategic, growth partnerships as part of our fast-paced distribution team right at the heart of Flock’s mission.

WHAT WE THINK IS MOST EXCITING ABOUT THE ROLE:

Be a part of building something truly game changing in the fleet market. You’ll manage a panel of key strategic brokers with significant growth opportunities. You’ll engage them on the market-leading benefits of Flock’s connected fleet proposition, and how together, we can reduce risk, improve costs and save lives. You’ll also have real freedom in how you use AI to work, whether that’s getting under the skin of a broker’s book before a meeting or spotting growth opportunities across your panel.

A LITTLE MORE ON WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

  • Act as a primary face of Flock for a panel of key broker partners, driving mutual growth and long-term success.

  • Deliver high volumes of broker submissions, directly supporting Flock’s ambitious growth targets.

  • Build, grow and develop our broker panel, onboarding new partners at pace and maximising their commercial potential.

  • Proactively engage brokers, finding new and creative ways to promote Flock’s appetite and proposition as we expand into new sectors.

  • Develop and execute clear, data-driven account growth strategies to drive sustained performance.

  • Achieve strong conversion and retention by supporting day-to-day trading activity and helping brokers (and Flock) win and retain business.

  • Work closely with internal teams, collaborating with brilliant Flockers across the business to deliver shared growth objectives.

  • Maintain strong broker advocacy by being visible, responsive and passionate about Flock’s product, proposition and mission.

  • Use AI in your day-to-day work, from broker research and meeting prep to analysing your pipeline, so your time goes on relationships rather than admin.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK:

ESSENTIAL

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience in managing broker relationships within the insurance sector, possessing a reputable standing in the industry.

  • Energy and innovation in abundance - the ability to work fast, spot opportunity and solve problems. 

  • A proven track record of exceeding revenue targets, driving business growth, and closely collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve collective objectives.

  • An existing network of broker contacts that will enable a rapid integration and immediate impact within Flock’s business development realm.

  • Exceptional understanding of the commercial broker marketplace, competitor carriers, broker business models, and processes.

  • Ability to deliver a consultative sales process, aligning Flock’s value proposition with brokers’ current and future business needs.

  • Comfortable using AI in your daily work, from research and meeting prep to account analysis, and curious about where else it could help you win business.

PREFERABLE

  • Experience building networks of brokers in a Commercial Motor Fleet setting. 

  • Have a broker distribution background with an active panel of brokers in the commercial insurance market. 

  • Can embrace new technologies and products, with experience of successfully distributing these to brokers.

WHAT WE OFFER (in addition to a competitive salary)

  • 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖 

  • Share Incentive Plan 📈

  • Workplace Pension 💰

  • Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

  • Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

  • Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

  • £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

  • £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

  • 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. Visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days.

ONE LAST THING..

Authenticity is important to us. We value the unique qualities and experiences you bring. So if you apply, just be your genuine self. It’s who we want!

raw.description:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

  •       Work with stakeholders on implementation of suitable IT controls and systems.

  •       Design, embed, and continuously audit Fractile’s internal compliance programme tailored to scale-up speed. Integrate compliance checks and export hold mechanisms into enterprise workflows. Develop and deliver practical, role-specific training regarding controlled technology transfers (deemed exports/re-exports).

  •       Maintain rigorous, audit-ready record-keeping systems for all exports, re-exports, and technical data transfers. Act as the primary operational contact for UK ECJU, HMRC, US BIS, and freight forwarders during compliance audits or shipping inquiries. Monitor regulatory updates targeting AI hardware, semiconductor supply chains, and sanctions to adjust operational processes rapidly.

Candidate Profile & Qualifications

  • Relevant Experience: 5+ years of dedicated trade compliance experience within a technology (ideally semiconductor) scale-up/multinational.

  • Domain Expertise: Practical, working mastery of both UK export control rules (ECJU) and US rules (deemed exports, foreign direct product rules, and sanctions regimes).

  • Technical Aptitude: Proven capability to translate complex technical hardware/software specs into precise ECCN classifications.

raw.description:
We're unlocking access to the NHS, because healthcare is not truly free until it's truly accessible 💙

The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works.

We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI.

We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly.

Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.

We operate from within a working GP practice in East London 🏥 We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe 🚀

⛩️ Our Principles

Exciting challenges lie ahead. Guided by our principles, we’ll meet these challenges with a thoughtful and caring approach. These principles drive everything we do at Healthtech-1:

  1. 💙 Care deeply

  2. 🏋️‍♀️ Work hard

  3. 🤝 Be your word

  4. 💬 Trust in radical truth and transparency

  5.  🚀 Do your life's best work

  6. 🥳 Find the fun

Read more about our principles and our "why" in the Healthtech-1 Handbook.

🎯 Goal expectations

As our Revenue Operations Manager, you’ll own the tooling and data that let’s Healthtech-1 scale across the NHS.

You’ll work closely across the GTM teams, deploy internal tooling with AI, turn Attio into our source of truth, and build an intelligent GTM motion on top.

This is an IC role, not a people management role. One week you might be rolling your sleeves up with the growth team, to be one or two steps ahead in identifying what the team need to hit their targets, and building internal tooling with AI to support the team. The next week you might be deep in the data, bringing company-wide data sources together to aide growth strategy planning e.g. identifying high demand areas in our marketplace, where we need to increase supply.

Objective 1: Keep systems and data running at a high standard

You will own and maintain Attio (our CRM), including its infrastructure, workflows and data hygiene across accounts and products. You will also own all our GTM tooling (e.g. Aircall, Calendly, Granola) and keep them running and improving. You will build a lot of tooling yourself using AI (e.g. dashboard, maps). You will run practice enrichment and data scraping pipelines so our data on customers stays current and usable.

Objective 2: Give the team and leadership clear visibility

You will build and maintain dashboards tracking company growth, cycle targets and product adoption. You will own reporting on practice numbers and growth trends. You will maintain tracking so leadership always has clear visibility on where deals are at.

Objective 3: Enable the growth team to sell more

The Growth team are your customer. You will build and maintain quality lead lists for AEs. You will support AEs with operational queries, targets and tooling. You will help new growth hires ramp faster through better tooling and playbooks.

Objective 4: Drive operational improvement

You will find and build automations and workflow improvements that save the team time. You will spot friction in how the growth team operates and fix it. You will actively look for ways to help the team drive more revenue.

⚠️ This role is not for everyone

This is a high-ownership, high-expectation role. You'll be working in a fast-moving healthtech environment where accuracy, speed, and proactivity all matter at the same time.

You probably won't enjoy this role if you:

  • Prefer to be told what to do over figuring out what to do

  • Treat ops as a support function rather than a growth lever

  • Aren't comfortable getting your hands dirty with data

  • Are content to maintain the status quo rather than improve it

  • Have never built things with AI

You will enjoy this role if you like owning systems end-to-end, building and deploying things with AI, and making the people around you more effective.

👍 Required experience

  • 2+ years in a revenue operations role in an early-stage startup, where you've owned systems, data and process improvement

  • Experience with Attio (or similar CRMs like HubSpot, Salesforce)

✅ Must-have traits

  • Great with AI - you know how to leverage AI well, whilst thoroughly checking accuracy

  • Detail oriented - you’re obsessed with the detail and CRM being the source of truth

  • Love data - you can build dashboards, spot trends, and make data useful for decision-making

  • Proactive problem solver - you don't wait for someone to flag a problem; you find it and fix it end-to-end.

  • Bias to action - you ship improvements quickly rather than over-planning

  • Team player - low ego, approachable and feedback-oriented; you get a kick from seeing the impact your work has on unlocking the sales team

  • Clear communicator - you keep stakeholders informed without being chased

💙 Desired traits

  • Comfortable with data scraping, enrichment tools and light automation (e.g. Zapier, Make, scripts)

  • Experience building dashboards and reports (e.g. Metabase, Looker, Google Sheets)

  • Familiarity with sales tooling (Calendly, Aircall, or equivalents)

  • Experience writing operational playbooks or onboarding materials

😊 The hiring process (4 stages)

  • 👋 Intro chat - with our Talent Partner, to learn more about each other

  • 📝 Take home task - complete a short task

  • 💼 An in-office work trial - work with the growth team on a real problem [1 day, fully paid]

  • ⛩️ Principles interview - with a Founder, to understand that our values align

  • 🎉 Offer!

💙 A bit about us

💙 We’re all NHS staff. We’re inside-outsiders. Trusted with one of the biggest datasets in the world.

🏥 Our office is within a GP practice. This is our unfair advantage. Got a question? Pop down the corridor. Want to learn how your work affects real patients? Pop downstairs to reception.

💪🏼 4 days in the office and 1 day WFH (for most roles). We highly prioritise in-person communication and prefer candidates who want to work 4+ days a week in the office. Our anchor days are Mon, Tues, Thurs and Fri. Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house every day when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🌀 We work in growth cycles. Every 8 weeks we do the same set of activities. 1 week outside of Business-as-Usual to research, strategise, plan our work. 7 weeks to knuckle down and deliver it.

🤝 We’re highly collaborative. One of the benefits of a high trust team is we often work autonomously, but as a team we’re very collaborative by nature. Two heads are often better than one, and we frequently lean on each other to solve problems together.

🤜🏽 We’re backed by industry leaders. We’re on the DigitalHealth.London Accelerator, backed by the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Program, winners of the London Business School Healthtech Challenge, Innovate UK, and Y Combinator (S23).

🚀 An opportunity for real upside

💉 Paid volunteer days. We offer an additional 2 paid days off per year where you can give back to your mission of choice.

🎢 Every 8 weeks we take a day off to socialise as a team. In the past we’ve hiked box hill, raved at All Points East and spent one rainy day at Thorpe park. This works out as 6 working days a year.

📚 Learning budget of £250 annually and time off to spend it - we care about this; this is flexible and based on need but everyone will receive a yearly allocation towards their continual growth.

🍽️ Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🥡 Team takeaways every Monday night

🥗 Health and fitness budget of £60 per month - see more here

🧘‍♂️ An additional 7 days of paid leave is available if you want to take time to learn how to meditate.

💫 Tooling; You’ll have your choice of operating systems and any additional tools you need to do your best work (e.g. keyboard, additional monitors, mouse etc). If you’re on our Engineering teams you’ll receive the latest MacBook Pro and our Growth & Ops teams receives a MacBook Air.

🩺 We know health and family come first which is why we have a generous sick leave policy with additional days that can be taken for mental health leave.

✈️ We prioritise time outside of work to bond, once a year we’ll holiday together! Destination chosen by popular vote. In 2025, we spent 8 days in a surf camp in France!

👎 No private medical insurance, because we believe in the NHS and we are here to improve it!

🐥 Parental leave: Post passing probation it is: statutory - 6 weeks 90% pay then, SMP for 33 weeks; if you've been an employee for a year: 12 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 27 weeks; and if you have been here for 2 years: 18 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 21 weeks. This will improve over time. We also include up to £9,000 of childcare contribution for primary caregivers to support a five-day return where possible.

👪 Fertility leave. We understand how difficult a fertility journey can be. This is why we give an extra 5 days off per year if you or your partner are going through fertility treatment.

🐖 Pension - We operate a standard 3% employer contribution and employees auto-contribute 5% of their salary. We use Nest as our provider.

🏡 Local living benefit - A one-off benefit to support living closer to the office: £5,000 if you live within a 30-minute walk, or £2,500 within a 30-minute bike. It is optional, available immediately on signing, and not linked to performance or progression.

🚕 If you choose to work late in the office, you can expense dinner after 7pm and an Uber home after 9pm, or earlier if you feel unsafe travelling in the dark. This is optional and about wellbeing, not performance or expectations.

⛵️And of course, an adventure of a lifetime!

🌈 Inclusive & Diverse by Design

We care about building a product that is loved and a culture that is rich in perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds.

Our team represents more than ten different cultures. We come together every lunch time for a home cooked meal, rotated among team members!

We want everyone in our team to know that they belong. We are purposeful about this and are proactively building a company that is inclusive of all people; from race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, neurodiversity, disability, colour, and national origin - essentially every type of diversity. We don’t just want people who fit in, we want them to fit together. We're active in continually improving the way we make this happen.

Senior Product Engineer
raw.description:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Engineering team

At hyperexponential, engineering is at the heart of our mission to transform the insurance industry. Our engineers build and scale, enabling insurers to model complex risks and make smarter pricing decisions at speed. By combining deep technical expertise with creativity, the team pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in insurance technology.

Within engineering, our product teams are cross-functional, pairing frontend and backend engineers with designers and product managers. This enables end-to-end ownership of features, with engineers contributing across design, architecture, implementation, and testing. Collaboration is a core part of how we work, ensuring that every release is both technically sound and valuable to our users.

About the role

Underwriters at the world's largest insurers still do much of their work in spreadsheets, email threads, and systems that were never designed for the decisions they are making. We are rebuilding that from the ground up.

You will join the Workflow Underwriting stream, building the next generation of our underwriting platform. This is not a platform with AI features bolted on. We are designing it around the agents we build, which means the architecture, the domain model, and the interaction patterns are all genuinely open questions. You will help answer them.

You will contribute at code, architecture, and domain level from your first weeks, and you will talk directly to the underwriters who use what you build.

 

What you’ll be doing

  • Design, build, and operate backend services in Kotlin or Java, and own them in production.

  • Turn ambiguous underwriting problems into simple, reliable software. Much of the work is deciding what to build, not just building it.

  • Shape architectural decisions: APIs, domain models, persistence, reliability, observability, and how the platform evolves without collapsing under its own weight.

  • Build real depth in the underwriting domain, to the point where you can challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.

  • Design and build agent-assisted workflows, and make judgement calls about where an agent should act, where it should advise, and where a human must stay in control.

  • Use AI coding tools, including Claude, as a core part of how you work. You delegate substantial work to them and you remain accountable for the quality, security, and correctness of everything you ship.

  • Work across boundaries with frontend engineers, product partners, and client-facing teams, and step outside your specialism when the problem demands it.

  • Give and take direct feedback, and raise the engineering bar around you.

 

What you’ll need to have done

  • Strong professional experience building and running backend systems in Kotlin, Java, or another JVM language.

  • Judgement in architecture and system design: a feel for what to build now, what to defer, and what will hurt in two years.

  • Evidence of shipping software that solved a real customer or business problem, ideally something you owned end to end.

  • A self-starting approach. You find the highest-value problem rather than waiting for a ticket.

  • Clear communication. You can hold the same conversation with an underwriter, an executive, and an engineer, and adjust for each.

  • Genuine appetite for problems with no known answer, and comfort working without a precedent to copy.

  • Confident, responsible use of AI coding tools, with a critical eye on their output.

  • Receptiveness to feedback. We give it directly and often, and we expect you to give it back.

 

Helpful, not required

  • Experience in insurance, underwriting, or another complex regulated domain. We will teach you the domain. We cannot teach curiosity about it.

  • Experience across both backend and frontend.

  • Experience building workflow, decision-support, or agent-assisted products.

  • Experience working directly with enterprise clients.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your talent partner will be able to share more details about this.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

 

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Manager Interview

  3. Technical Assessment (e.g., code review, system design)

  4. Values Interview

  5. Meet the CEO

  6. We offer!

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

  • Design, build, and operate backend services in Kotlin or Java, and own them in production.

  • Turn ambiguous underwriting problems into simple, reliable software. Much of the work is deciding what to build, not just building it.

  • Shape architectural decisions: APIs, domain models, persistence, reliability, observability, and how the platform evolves without collapsing under its own weight.

  • Build real depth in the underwriting domain, to the point where you can challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.

  • Design and build agent-assisted workflows, and make judgement calls about where an agent should act, where it should advise, and where a human must stay in control.

  • Use AI coding tools, including Claude, as a core part of how you work. You delegate substantial work to them and you remain accountable for the quality, security, and correctness of everything you ship.

  • Work across boundaries with frontend engineers, product partners, and client-facing teams, and step outside your specialism when the problem demands it.

  • Give and take direct feedback, and raise the engineering bar around you.

 

What you’ll need to have done

  • Strong professional experience building and running backend systems in Kotlin, Java, or another JVM language.

  • Judgement in architecture and system design: a feel for what to build now, what to defer, and what will hurt in two years.

  • Evidence of shipping software that solved a real customer or business problem, ideally something you owned end to end.

  • A self-starting approach. You find the highest-value problem rather than waiting for a ticket.

  • Clear communication. You can hold the same conversation with an underwriter, an executive, and an engineer, and adjust for each.

  • Genuine appetite for problems with no known answer, and comfort working without a precedent to copy.

  • Confident, responsible use of AI coding tools, with a critical eye on their output.

  • Receptiveness to feedback. We give it directly and often, and we expect you to give it back.

 

Helpful, not required

  • Experience in insurance, underwriting, or another complex regulated domain. We will teach you the domain. We cannot teach curiosity about it.

  • Experience across both backend and frontend.

  • Experience building workflow, decision-support, or agent-assisted products.

  • Experience working directly with enterprise clients.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your talent partner will be able to share more details about this.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

 

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Manager Interview

  3. Technical Assessment (e.g., code review, system design)

  4. Values Interview

  5. Meet the CEO

  6. We offer!

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

Infinite Lambda is a multi-award-winning Services-as-Software company specialising in enterprise data and AI transformation. We help leading enterprises create scalable AI capabilities that drive meaningful impact across the organisation.

We are in it for the long run. This means nurturing sustainable growth, creating trustworthy technology, and empowering the people who use it.

 

Locations & Work arrangements

The role is remote, but you will be expected to travel occasionally to client sites, company meetings, and partner events.

raw.description:
Applied AI Engineer - Direct Acquisition

We're planning this as a six-month secondment. There may be an opportunity to extend it or make it permanent.

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join the Direct Acquisition team.

You'll design and build AI agents that run whole business processes, from planning the work to learning from the results. What you find will steer how far iwoca takes agents across the business.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

Direct Acquisition includes iwoca's Marketing, Sales, Brand and Acquisition Tech teams. Together, they reach UK businesses of all shapes and sizes through paid and organic marketing channels and direct sales.

A new team in Direct Acquisition builds agents that automate and improve acquisition processes. That's its only focus, and it works closely with Acquisition Tech. It's small – a product owner and you – and everyone builds. You'll report to the Head of Direct Acquisition, who sets the commercial direction.

The role

As the Applied AI Engineer, you'll build the agents and the systems around them. Most of the work is system design and backend engineering.

You'll start with direct mail. The first goal is an agent that plans each monthly round, uses iwoca's existing predictive models to build the mailing file, and learns from the results as they come in. The pattern is simple to say and hard to get right: the agent orchestrates, deterministic code does the work, and a human in the loop approves the file before it goes to print. You'll work with the people who run each process to understand the edge cases, and with Core Systems and Compliance on access and controls.

The agents don't exist yet, and much is still open: which processes the team takes on, and what the architecture looks like. You'll own those design decisions and write most of the code yourself, much of it with AI coding tools. Some of this won't work, and finding out why is one of the main outputs of the role.

  • Architecture. You'll design what agents need to run reliably: memory that persists between runs, task management, access to tools, permissions, and a record of every decision and why. You'll build each piece so the next process can reuse it.

  • Guardrails. You'll decide where the agent uses judgement and where code enforces rules the agent can't change, like suppressions, compliance checks and budget limits.

  • Delivery. You'll own each agent end to end: connect it to iwoca's predictive models, data pipelines and channel tools, and run it alongside the current process until it has shown it works.

  • Measurement. You'll track how often agents need a person, where they fail, what they cost, and what they're worth.

The requirements

We're looking for the depth of someone who has solved hard problems, and the pace of someone who moves fast in areas that are new to them.

Essential:

  • System ownership. You've owned a complex system end to end, from design to running it in production, and lived with the consequences of your architecture choices.

  • Design judgement. You've made architecture decisions other people built on, and you can explain the trade-offs and what you'd change. When an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.

  • Pace. You've got things live quickly in unfamiliar areas and they kept working once people relied on them.

  • Agent engineering. You've built systems where LLMs take actions – more than chat or summaries – and you can explain what went wrong and how you fixed it. You know when a problem needs an agent and when it needs a for-loop.

  • Controls. You've built permissions, data access rules and audit trails into systems from the start.

  • Constructive challenge. You work well with commercial and product colleagues, and when an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.

  • AI leverage. You've used AI coding tools to produce engineering work you couldn't have delivered without them – a service, an integration, or an internal tool others use. You have opinions on how to get the most out of them, and you check their output before it reaches production.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Languages and data tools. You've worked with Python, Go, Snowflake or dbt.

  • Evaluation. You've built evals that measure how an agent performs and where it fails.

  • Marketing and growth tech. You've worked with ad platforms, CRMs or direct mail.

  • Quantitative foundations. You come from a numerical or technical field, such as physics, engineering, maths or computer science.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days' holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we've been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Compensation: £80K – £100K

raw.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with.

We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services.

We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow.

Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling.


How we work:

  • We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway.

  • We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from.

  • We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.

  • We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end.

The role

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

Impact and influence

  • Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate.

  • Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build.

  • Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders.

  • AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them.

  • Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them.

The requirements

Essential skills

  • Experience. Experience in data protection or privacy operations, or in a compliance, legal, risk or operational role where data protection was a real part of the job.

  • Data protection knowledge. A solid practical understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR, and of how the ICO expects firms to apply them. Familiarity with the changes made by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 is an advantage.

  • Privacy operations and assessments. Hands-on experience of statutory work: DSARs, DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments, breach handling, ROPA maintenance or data processing agreement review. You may not have done all of these — but we want to see that you have done some of them properly.

  • AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.

  • Stakeholder management: Comfortable dealing directly with product, engineering, marketing, credit and operations teams, and able to give a non-specialist a clear answer they can act on rather than a legal summary.

Bonus:

  • Sector experience. Financial services or fintech, ideally in lending or payments.

  • Credentials. A privacy or AI qualification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, or ICO-recognised practitioner certificates — or working towards one.

  • Practical tooling. Experience using Claude Code, LLMs or privacy management platforms.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

raw.description:
Data Scientist - Broker Terms Team

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the Broker Terms team.

You'll shape the analytical approach for a team that sets the terms on iwoca's biggest acquisition channel. The team is young, with many unexplored opportunities.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they ildrive.

The team

Broker Terms is a growing team that sits within iwoca's third-party acquisition department. It owns the full offer terms strategy for customers referred through the broker network – both first-time customers and repeat. The team sets pricing, loan amounts, durations, and broker commissions, and owns the UX that presents them to brokers and customers.

The team is small and interdisciplinary, combining commercial strategy, engineering, and data science. The work translates business questions into quantitative problems, and findings into actionable decisions. Active projects include:

  • Model-based pricing – creating a sophisticated model to offer bespoke pricing to each customer

  • A no-fee test – examining how our product performs when we remove all drawdown fees, and how that influence customer repayment behaviour

  • Testing longer-duration flexi-loan products with particular customer segments.

  • Reintroductions - exploring the right offer terms to give returning customers

The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use.

The role

You'll model expected customer take-up rates, design experiments, and translate findings into pricing and product decisions for the acquisition channel that drives the most customer lifetime value (CLTV). Because the Broker Terms team is a young team, you'll influence how its analytical approach develops, not just what it produces.

The work has direct commercial consequences: brokers act on what the team builds and tests, and that shapes which customers iwoca wins and on what terms.

  • Offer terms and experimentation. You'll model how customers respond to offer terms and how brokers make decisions under uncertainty. You'll design experiments where causal inference is central: you'll need to know where standard A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead.

  • Commercial translation. You'll work with commercial and strategy colleagues and see your analysis applied directly in day-to-day decisions. That includes meeting brokers in person – gaining context that shapes how you frame and interpret results – and coordinating with adjacent teams responsible for underwriting decisions, repeat lending, and offer construction.

  • CLTV and customer journey. You'll think across the full broker-referred customer journey – from first funding to repeat – identifying what drives CLTV and what changes to offer terms or UX improve it. You own both the strategy and the mechanism, so your findings feed directly into what the team builds and tests.

  • AI and ways of working. You'll use AI to accelerate and automate your analytical work – not occasionally, but as a default. You should have a view on where it genuinely helps and where a different approach is better.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work.

  • Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. You have experience with careful experimental design to facilitate clean, trustworthy results.

  • Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it.

  • Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries (pandas, numpy, sklearn, PyMC).

  • AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – an analysis pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't, and you check its output before anyone acts on it.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in commercial and strategy roles.

Bonus:

  • Modelling depth. You've built or adapted statistical or ML models and can explain the maths behind them to commercial stakeholders.

  • Stochastic methods. You've used stochastic processes for inference or time-series modelling.

  • Broker market insight. You've worked with brokers or other intermediaries in lending or financial services.

The salary

We expect to pay from £70,000 to £100,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

This is an opportunity to build your career in communications at a fast-growing fintech that's reshaping SME finance. You'll be part of iwoca's external communications team, helping drive coverage across our expanding product portfolio, working on data-led campaigns and supporting our work with government and policymakers.

Our comms function works across the business to position iwoca as a leading voice in SME finance. You'll collaborate closely with Product, Commercial, and Executive teams to translate business priorities into compelling narratives that drive both brand awareness and customer acquisition.

The role

We're looking for a Communications Executive with up to two years' experience to join our UK comms team. You'll also help with the BAU media activities that keep iwoca front-of-mind with key journalists and stakeholders.

raw.description:
About Juicebox

Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war.

In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose.

Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies.

We are on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth, powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world.

Juicebox has raised over $116M in funding from lead investors including Sequoia Capital, DST Global, and NFDG. Read more about our $80M Series B here. Additional investors in Juicebox include Y Combinator, Coatue, Bond, Lux, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital.

About the Role

As an Account Executive at Juicebox, you'll play a foundational role in launching our London office and building our go-to-market presence across Europe. As one of our first Account Executives in the region, you'll have the opportunity to shape our sales motion, influence how we serve European customers, and help establish Juicebox as a leader in AI-powered recruiting.

Our go-to-market motion is highly product-led. We generate 200+ inbound demo requests every month through our free trial and demo experience, giving you the opportunity to focus on building relationships and closing business rather than generating outbound pipeline. You'll sell primarily to Talent Acquisition, People, and Recruiting leaders, while also expanding relationships across our growing base of 2,000+ customers. We move quickly, with typical sales cycles of just 2 to 3 weeks, and consistently win against legacy recruiting solutions.

You Will…

  • Own the full sales cycle from discovery through negotiation and close across the European market.

  • Help establish and scale Juicebox's go-to-market presence as part of our founding London team.

  • Convert inbound demo requests and free trial users into long-term customers.

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition, People, and Recruiting leaders to understand their hiring challenges and recommend solutions.

  • Identify expansion opportunities within our growing customer base.

  • Collaborate closely with marketing, customer success, and product to refine our European go-to-market strategy.

  • Maintain accurate pipeline forecasts and CRM hygiene.

  • Share customer insights to help shape our product roadmap and regional growth strategy.

You Have…

  • 2+ years of experience closing SaaS deals.

  • Experience selling deals with annual contract values (ACVs) between £10,000 and £50,000.

  • A track record of consistently exceeding quota (President's Club, Top Performer, Top 10%, MVP, or similar achievements).

  • Strong discovery, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.

  • Excellent communication skills and a customer-first mindset.

  • A bias toward action and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment.

  • Located in or willing to relocate to London.

Bonus Points If You…

  • You've sold to Talent Acquisition, People, HR, or Recruiting leaders.

  • You have experience in a product-led growth (PLG) sales environment.

  • You've worked on a small, high-performing GTM team where ownership and collaboration were critical.

  • You have experience selling AI, recruiting, or HR technology solutions.

Perks & Benefits for all Full Time Employees

  • Top-of-market compensation with meaningful equity, because everyone should share in our success.

  • Daily meals provided: breakfast catering, lunch order via DoorDash corporate, and for those who like to work late, dinner if staying after 7pm

For US Employees:

  • Comprehensive healthcare with 100% employer-paid medical coverage for employees (PPO Platinum plan with $0 deductible). 90% employer contribution for dependents. Dental & Vision: 90% employer covered; 85% for dependents.

  • $2,000 annual wellness stipend to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being.

  • $300/month commuting stipend to help cover the cost of getting to and from the office.

For UK Employees:

  • Comprehensive private medical insurance with £0 excess, full outpatient cover, comprehensive cancer care, mental health treatment, and 24/7 GP access.

  • £1,500 annual wellness stipend to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being

  • £3,500/year commuting stipend to help cover the cost of getting to and from the office.

Compensation: £130K – £190K • Offers Equity • Offers Commission

raw.description:
THE COMPANY:

Juul Labs's mission is to transition the world's billion adult smokers away from combustible cigarettes, eliminate their use, and combat underage usage of our products. We have the opportunity to address one of the world's most intractable challenges through a commitment to exceptional quality, research, design, and innovation. Backed by leading technology investors, we are committed to the same excellence when it comes to hiring great talent.

We are a diverse team that is united by this common purpose and we are hiring the world's best engineers, scientists, designers, product managers, operations experts, and customer service and business professionals. If the opportunity to build your career is compelling, read on for more details.

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Reporting to the Head of Field Sales, the Senior City Development Manager is the lead field operator for key strategic cities. Bringing strong commercial experience, this hands-on role combines city strategy, regional key account management, and specialist product knowledge to ensure field activity is tailored, scaled, and executed effectively. As well as taking primary ownership of their own city performance - driving awareness, distribution, trade execution, and market share - the role provides commercial coaching and practical support to City Development Managers across the region.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Commercial Delivery & Strategic Customer Management

  • Account Management: Take ownership of regional key account operators and on-the-ground route-to-market partnerships. Build strong commercial relationships that drive long-term growth across distribution, execution, education, and rate-of-sale.
  • Commercial Coaching: Act as a commercial sounding board for City Development Managers. Offer practical advice, coaching, and support on account planning, negotiating, and working through local trade challenges.
  • Commercial Tools: Create, refine, and deploy practical commercial sales tools (e.g., commercial calculators, regional activity, customer and channel propositions) that address ground-level field challenges and help field teams and CDMs win across regions.
  • Regional Development: Build relationships and develop non-traditional trade channels, tailoring the approach to fit local market nuances while ensuring all partnerships align with company goals and regulatory requirements.
  • Execution Standards: Set the operational benchmark for distribution, brand visibility, and advocacy across all trade channels (including priority regional accounts, Wholesale, Vape, and alternative channels). Measure and evaluate execution quality across key cities, establishing clear guidelines and sharing proven approaches to help CDMs elevate standards across their own territories.

City Strategy & Execution

  • City Strategy: Adapt national frameworks into practical, city-specific plans that reflect local demographics, trade setups, and regional key account footprints. Identify what each specific city needs to win, ensuring resources are deployed effectively.
  • CDM Guidance: support CDMs in analysing their own cities, adapting national plans to fit their city's specific dynamics, and executing tailored activity efficiently. 
  • Third-Party Prioritisation: Work alongside and co-ordinate third-party field teams on a city-by-city basis, making sure field resources are directed to where the local opportunity is greatest.
  • Events & Activations: Identify and execute local promotional activity and trade programmes, designed specifically around the local target audience to drive engagement, product education, and sales.
  • Performance Ownership: drive city performance and manage risks and opportunities in your region
  • Field Insight & Strategy: Link field execution with the Head of Field Sales by translating plans into action, while feeding back trade realities, competitor moves, and new channel opportunities to shape national strategy.

YOUR PROFILE: Personal and Professional Qualifications

  • 3-5 years' experience in a similar role or commercial setting
  • Commercial Acumen & Account Management: Strong track record in account management alongside experience handling multi-site accounts that span across adjacent territories. Proven ability to negotiate, drive sales volume, distribution, and market share. Ability to adapt style to both existing and new channels and opportunities. 
  • Commercial Coaching & Regional Influence: Proven ability to influence and mentor peers by sharing commercial expertise, guiding regional key account negotiations, and helping tailor city plans, all while supporting established line-management structures.
  • Commercial Tools: Experience developing practical sales tools and toolkits to solve local trade challenges and drive regional growth.
  • Execution & Quality Evaluation: Skilled at turning ideas into reality by tailoring local activations, brand, and direct engagement opportunities to fit specific city needs. Proven ability to measure and evaluate sales return, and provide analysis to inform future execution standards
  • Commercial Analysis & Problem Solving: Skilled at analysing city sales data and trade trends to spot commercial gaps, fix underperforming territories, and feed clear market feedback to the Head of Field Sales.
  • Self-Driven & Resilient: Challenges the status quo, takes decisive action, and turns ideas into commercial results in changing environments. 
  • A full UK driving licence is required for this role. 
  • Education: BA/BS degree preferred but not required

JUUL LABS PERKS & BENEFITS: 

  • A place to grow your career. We'll help you set big goals - and exceed them
  • People. Work with talented, committed and supportive teammates
  • Equity and performance bonuses. Every employee is a stakeholder in our success
  • Location. Field based with a requirement to be in the London office when required
Juul Labs is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment for all employees and job applicants, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. Juul Labs also complies with the employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act. All applicants must have authorization to work for Juul Labs in the US.

raw.title: AI Ops Engineer (Business Operations)
raw.description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 10x YoY.

The Role

We’re looking for an AI Ops Engineer to build the internal systems that help Kernel scale without adding unnecessary manual work. You’ll work across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations - finding the highest-leverage problems and building practical AI-powered workflows.

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll take ideas from a vague business problem to a tool or workflow that people use, then maintain and improve it in production. You’ll choose the fastest sensible approach for each problem - coding agents, automation platforms, APIs, data pipelines or lightweight code.

You’ll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations, and partner closely with GTM, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define how an AI-native company operates: help build Kernel’s internal playbook for using AI across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations

  • Make our GTM team more productive: automate the repetitive work in prospecting, account research, meeting prep and CRM hygiene, so BDRs, AEs and Account Managers spend more time with customers

  • Build internal tools and workflows: use coding agents, APIs, automation platforms, no-code tools or lightweight code

  • Turn company data into operational leverage: connect and improve data across our systems, then put it to work in AI agents, proactive workflows and better decision-making

  • Put AI agents to work across Kernel: give teams agents with the right context, tools and guardrails so they can move faster without sacrificing judgement or reliability

  • Be Kernel’s own internal customer: deploy Kernel on Kernel’s CRM, improve our GTM data and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering

  • Level up the team: help colleagues become confident AI users, document what works and turn successful experiments into repeatable ways of working

Your First 6 Months

For your first six months, you’ll focus on our sales team. You’ll sit with our BDRs, AEs and Account Managers and learn how they work day to day. Then you’ll automate everything that doesn’t need a human. That means going deep on Salesforce and our GTM stack, and owning the RevOps workflows behind them. After that, you’ll bring the same approach to Marketing, Customer Success and Operations.

What You Bring

  • A track record of shipping: you’ve built tools, automations or AI workflows that people use every day, ideally inside a small, fast-moving startup. Around 2–5 years of experience is typical, but what you’ve built matters more than your years. Ex-founders welcome

  • Experience inside a high-growth startup, or building your own, is highly desirable

  • Curious about sales: you’re keen to learn how our BDRs and AEs work, and how Salesforce is set up, before you build for them

  • AI-tool obsessed: you are constantly testing new models, agents, MCPs and workflows, and you have the judgement to turn them into reliable systems that people actually adopt

  • Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented, messy information into reliable workflows and create feedback loops that keep it trustworthy

  • Can’t unsee inefficiency: you see the company as a connected system; when you find a broken or unnecessarily manual process, your instinct is to understand it, build the fix and make sure it sticks

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Prefer deep specialization over breadth: this role means switching between projects and teams, depending on business needs

  • Prefer steady-state work over project-based sprints: priorities will shift as the business evolves

  • Only want “strategic” work: you will personally build the tools, clean the data and fix the workflows

❌ This role is definitely not for you if you:

  • Need every task to be clearly scoped before starting: ambiguity and learning on the fly are constant

  • Avoid operational grunt work or lose interest after the prototype

  • Want to protect a 9-to-6 or a mostly remote setup: we are in the office together 4–5 days a week and the pace is high

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 💰 Salary: £60,000–£85,000 + equity

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🥕 £450 monthly office dinner allowance

  • ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere

  • 🍼 Generous parental leave policy

  • 💼 Pension plan

  • 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office

  • 🎉 Team events and dinners

  • 🚀 Work directly with the founders to deploy AI across a fast-growing company

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

❤️ Team

Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations

Amin Shafi, BizOps Associate

Dave Bentham, Head of Sales

🎫 Visas & Relocation

Not offered for this role.

Interview Process

  • Stage 1: Screening - Intro call

  • Stage 2: Technical - In-person case interview

  • Stage 3: Coffee chat - In-person discussion with members of our GTM team

  • Final Stage: Values - Interview with founders for culture and values alignment

If there is mutual fit, we move to references and offer.

Compensation: £60K – £85K • Offers Equity

The Role

We’re looking for an AI Ops Engineer to build the internal systems that help Kernel scale without adding unnecessary manual work. You’ll work across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations - finding the highest-leverage problems and building practical AI-powered workflows.

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll take ideas from a vague business problem to a tool or workflow that people use, then maintain and improve it in production. You’ll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations, and partner closely with GTM, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define how an AI-native company operates: help build Kernel’s internal playbook for using AI across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations

  • Make our GTM team more productive: automate the repetitive work in prospecting, account research, meeting prep and CRM hygiene, so BDRs, AEs and Account Managers spend more time with customers

  • Build internal tools and workflows: use coding agents, APIs, automation platforms, no-code tools or lightweight code

  • Turn company data into operational leverage: connect and improve data across our systems, then put it to work in AI agents, proactive workflows and better decision-making

  • Put AI agents to work across Kernel: give teams agents with the right context, tools and guardrails so they can move faster without sacrificing judgement or reliability

  • Be Kernel’s own internal customer: deploy Kernel on Kernel’s CRM, improve our GTM data and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering

  • Level up the team: help colleagues become confident AI users, document what works and turn successful experiments into repeatable ways of working

Your First 6 Months

What You Bring

  • AI-tool obsessed: you are constantly testing new models, agents, MCPs and workflows, and you have the judgement to turn them into reliable systems that people actually adopt

  • Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented, messy information into reliable workflows and create feedback loops that keep it trustworthy

  • Can’t unsee inefficiency: you see the company as a connected system; when you find a broken or unnecessarily manual process, your instinct is to understand it, build the fix and make sure it sticks
