raw.title: Account Executive SMB (German)
raw.description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

As an Account Executive, you manage a territory that includes target-accounts and an existing book of business with companies up to 1,000 employees. Your primary focus is hunting new business opportunities, building sales pipeline, and driving growth within the SMB sector. You are also responsible for upselling into the existing account base, leveraging our Extended Access Management platform. You will own a specific geographical region or country within the EMEA market.

How we’re using AI today

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

Expectations of this role
This is a hybrid role. You will be expected to work from 1Password's London office 3 days per week, with the flexibility to work from the office up to 5 days based on business needs.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.

What we're looking for:

  • 2+ years of SaaS sales experience, preferably in security with a focus on SMB or Mid Market accounts OR a top performing BDR with outbound experience and success ready to step up.

  • Fluent in German; written and spoken

  • Experience owning a geographical territory or country within EMEA.

  • Proven track record of meeting or exceeding sales quotas and KPIs.

  • Experience upselling & cross-selling to both new customers and across a book of business

  • Solid skills in:

    • Prospecting, pipeline building, account planning, value-based selling, and territory management, with effective operating rigor in pipeline management, forecasting, and pacing to target

    • Business acumen, solution selling, negotiation, & presenting to company decision makers/stakeholders

    • Written and verbal communication skills across email and communication tools such as Slack, and Zoom, with the ability to make technical concepts accessible to non-technical parties.

  • Demonstrated ability to understand and articulate complex cybersecurity concepts, particularly in Identity and Access Management.

  • Resilient, self-motivated, and committed to achieving targets while thriving in a remote environment.

  • A proven team player, eager to collaborate and achieve shared goals rather than working in isolation.

  • Curious and coachable, with a proven ability to apply feedback, adapt, and continuously improve.

  • Preferred: Proficiency with Salesforce, Slack, Zoom, Linkedin Sales Navigator & Outreach

  • Willingness to travel within your region for client meetings and industry events.

What you can expect:

  • Own Your Territory: Manage and grow your designated geographical region or country within EMEA, focusing on acquiring new SMB clients and expanding existing accounts.

  • Manage Pipeline: Build and maintain a healthy sales pipeline through proactive prospecting, inbound leads, cold calling, and networking, utilizing our formalized sales process, MEDDPPICC.

  • Drive New Business Growth: Achieve or exceed sales targets and KPIs by:

    • Consistently meeting or exceeding monthly/quarterly sales quotas.

    • Maintaining a high level of outbound activity, including calls, emails, and meetings.

    • Developing and closing new business opportunities within your territory.

  • Drive Organic Growth: Identify opportunities to upsell 1Password solutions within existing accounts, leveraging your understanding of Extended Access Management.

  • Engage the Industry: Attend industry events, trade shows, and conferences to represent 1Password, build brand presence, and network with potential customers

  • Stay Informed: Stay up to date on cybersecurity trends and developments, particularly in Identity and Access Management, to effectively position 1Password solutions and communicate their value to prospects.

  • Collaborate Cross-Functionally:

    • Build collaborative relationships with internal teams (e.g. BDR, Solutions, Channels, Onboarding, Customer Success) to optimize client engagement and identify growth opportunities.

    • Engage in multi-threaded relationships within client organizations to enhance overall account health.

  • Focus on Solution Selling:

    • Implement selling strategies to align our solutions with client needs and objectives.

    • Demonstrate a deep understanding of client pain points and position our offerings as strategic solutions.

  • Present and Negotiate:

    • Confidently present to company decision makers/stakeholders, articulating the value proposition of our products and services.

    • Create mutual action plans to align the sales team and prospects on responsibilities, steps and timelines for closing deals.

    • Utilize effective negotiation skills to drive mutually beneficial outcomes.

UK-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between £44,000 GBP and £62,000 GBP, and is commission-eligible. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, pension, and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.


At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.


Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.


Our approach to work
We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement.

For all roles, occasional travel may be required. This includes things like: department-wide offsites, quarterly department meetings and periodic customer events. These events are typically held in varying locations across Canada, USA and/or EMEA. In leadership roles, you can expect to travel once per month on average.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.


What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

Health and wellbeing
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy

Growth and future
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

Community
🤝 Paid volunteer days
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
*Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.

You belong here.

1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.

Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at ----- and we’ll work to meet your needs.

Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you.

Successful applicants will be required to complete a background check that may consist of prior employment verification, reference checks, education confirmation, criminal background, publicly available social media, credit history, or other information, as permitted by local law.

raw.description:
Deployment Strategist, AI Solutions

London, with travel to NYC and client sites

Who A.Team is?

A.Team builds the agentic operating system for the enterprise. Every company is being told AI will change how it works, and few are seeing it happen. We’re here to change that. We build AI systems that capture what a company knows as work happens, carry it across teams and decisions, and get smarter with every outcome. We pair them with top AI talent who embed with our customers to make sure those systems get adopted and keep improving. Today we’re focused on consumer packaged goods. Global CPG marketing teams use A.Team to act on cultural trends as they happen, optimize campaigns and media spend, and turn commercial and pricing signals into clear decisions. We’re proven in production with Fortune 500 brands and partner with Google Cloud, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI.

About the Role

We're looking for an experienced enterprise transformation and delivery leader to own the end-to-end success of one of A.Team's most strategic enterprise clients.

You will lead a complex, multi-workstream AI transformation program, working closely with senior client executives and A.Team's product, engineering, and delivery teams. Your responsibility is to translate business priorities into an actionable roadmap, drive execution across teams, ensure successful adoption, and deliver measurable business impact.

This is a highly visible leadership role that combines strategic thinking, hands-on execution, and executive relationship management. You will be the single point of accountability for the overall success of the client program—from defining priorities and aligning stakeholders to ensuring solutions are delivered, adopted, and generating value.

You'll work closely with the Account Executive, who owns the commercial relationship, renewals, and expansion, while you own delivery execution and client outcomes.

We're looking for someone who has successfully led large-scale enterprise transformation or technology implementation programs, can navigate complex organizations, and knows how to turn ambitious strategies into real-world results.

What You'll Do

  • Own End-to-End Client Delivery: Take full accountability for the successful delivery of a strategic enterprise client program, from defining priorities and planning through implementation, adoption, and measurable business impact. Ensure all workstreams deliver against agreed objectives, timelines, and quality standards.

  • Lead Cross-Functional Execution: Coordinate product, engineering, PMs, and AIOps teams to deliver as one integrated program. Set priorities, manage dependencies and risks, resolve escalations, and ensure clear ownership and accountability across teams.

  • Define and Drive the Deployment Roadmap: Work with client stakeholders to translate business objectives into a prioritized roadmap of AI use cases. Identify high-impact opportunities, validate them quickly with our Pathfinder team, and continuously evolve the roadmap based on business needs and results.

  • Ensure Successful Implementation: Oversee the deployment of AI solutions, from initial pilots through production rollout and ongoing operations. Proactively identify and remove blockers, manage delivery risks, and ensure solutions meet both business and technical requirements.

  • Drive Adoption and Change Management: Ensure deployed solutions become embedded in the client's day-to-day workflows. Work with business stakeholders to drive organizational alignment, overcome resistance, address training needs, and maximize adoption.

  • Deliver Measurable Business Value: Define success metrics and business cases for each initiative. Track performance, adoption, and ROI, ensuring the program delivers tangible business outcomes rather than simply shipping technology.

  • Lead Executive Stakeholder Relationships: Serve as the primary delivery counterpart to senior client executives. Build trusted relationships, align stakeholders across functions, manage expectations, lead executive reviews, and navigate complex organizational dynamics.

  • Partner with the Account Executive: Work closely with the AE, who owns the commercial relationship, renewals, and expansion. Surface new opportunities, provide evidence of delivered value, and ensure alignment between client priorities, delivery commitments, and commercial objectives.

  • Build a Scalable Delivery Playbook: Capture lessons learned, establish best practices, and develop repeatable processes that can be applied across future enterprise deployments.

Must-Haves

  • Enterprise Transformation Leadership: 8+ years of experience leading large-scale digital transformation, technology implementation, or innovation programs for major enterprises. You've owned complex programs from strategy through execution and delivered measurable business outcomes. Experience may come from management consulting, enterprise technology companies, or in-house transformation leadership. This is the most important requirement for the role.

  • End-to-End Program Ownership: Proven ability to lead complex, multi-workstream programs, coordinating cross-functional teams, managing competing priorities, resolving dependencies, and driving execution. You take full accountability for outcomes, even when teams don't report directly to you.

  • Executive Stakeholder Management: A track record of building trusted relationships with senior enterprise executives, navigating complex organizations, aligning stakeholders with competing interests, and influencing decisions. You're equally comfortable in the boardroom and working hands-on with delivery teams.

  • AI and Technical Fluency: Strong understanding of how enterprise AI and technology solutions are designed, built, integrated, deployed, and operated. You can engage confidently with engineers and technical leaders, challenge assumptions, evaluate trade-offs, and translate technical complexity into business implications. You don't need to be an engineer.

  • Business Acumen and Value Realization: Ability to translate business objectives into actionable plans, define meaningful success metrics, build compelling business cases, and demonstrate measurable value through adoption, operational improvements, and ROI.

  • Decisiveness and Problem-Solving: Strong judgment and a bias for action. You can navigate ambiguity, make difficult trade-offs, resolve complex problems, and keep teams focused on what matters most.

  • London-Based: Based in London, with the ability to work on-site with enterprise clients and travel to New York and other client locations as needed.

Nice-to-Haves

  • CPG, marketing or commercial-function experience

  • Experience driving adoption of AI or agentic tools inside large enterprises

  • Experience at an early-stage company where you built the playbook, not just ran it

  • Background spanning consulting and product or delivery leadership

raw.title: Product Associate
raw.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We're expanding access to affordable credit by launching credit products that make a real difference to customers. We move quickly, often with leading fintech, consumer and e-commerce companies, so that we can offer affordable credit at the right point in the customer journey. We work in a highly regulated environment, so our products have to work end to end from day one: technically, operationally and commercially.

 

As a Product Associate, you'll work across product, data and commercials. You'll dig into how our products perform, from funnel conversion to loan-level unit economics, and turn what you find into ideas for how we scale, improve margins and grow. You'll work hands-on with data and code, alongside Product Managers, Engineering, Credit and Operations. You'll help decide where the product goes next, as well as how we ship it.

 

This role is for top-tier STEM or Economics graduates who think like analysts, build like engineers and care about the P&L like owners, and who want to progress to Product Manager at a fast-growing, industry-leading fintech.

 

What you'll be doing

 

Product analytics & insight

  • Own analysis of product performance across the full funnel: traffic, applications, approvals, conversion, originations, repayment and credit outcomes

  • Build and maintain the dashboards, metrics and data models that Product, Credit and Operations rely on

  • Form sharp hypotheses, design experiments (journey changes, pricing, A/B tests) and measure the impact rigorously

  • Get to the root cause of anomalies quickly, whether the cause is in the data, the code or the customer journey

Unit economics & commercial thinking

  • Model the economics of each product: acquisition cost, approval and take-up rates, pricing, funding cost, expected loss, servicing cost and lifetime value

  • Put numbers on the trade-offs behind product decisions, such as wider approval versus higher losses, or partner revenue share versus volume

  • Track contribution margin and cohort profitability by product, channel and partner, and show where we make or lose money

Growth & product strategy

  • Come up with ideas for scaling and growing from where we are today (new segments, channels, products and pricing) and estimate what each one is worth

  • Look across our products and partnerships for places where they reinforce each other: cross-sell, top-ups, repeat lending, shared customers and shared data

  • Help evaluate new partner opportunities and build the business case, covering volume, economics, integration effort and risk

  • Turn the strongest ideas into clear proposals and see them through to launch

Building & shipping

  • Use AI coding tools to build and ship product end to end, across both front-end and back-end, from quick prototypes to features that go live

  • Build internal tools, automations and data workflows that remove manual work and help the team move faster

  • Be proficient with our analytics stack: build dashboards in AWS QuickSight and track funnels, events and experiments in PostHog

  • Use SQL and Python every day to pull, model and analyse data

  • Learn how our APIs, decisioning flows and data pipelines work, and work directly with engineers on specs, testing and release validation

  • Support Product Managers with discovery, delivery and partner onboarding

Launch readiness & operations

  • Define success criteria for each launch and the metrics that show whether it's working

  • Design test scenarios, including edge cases and failure modes, and test the end-to-end customer journey before release

  • Work closely with QA to make sure production releases are stable

  • Monitor production performance after release, and pick up and triage related bugs with engineering

  • Make sure new products and journeys work at launch for customer support, collections and complaints teams

  • Use operational data to spot recurring issues, fix them at the source and make sure they're closed out, not just discussed

Who you are

raw.title: Product Lead
raw.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The Role

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality.

  • Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition.

  • Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

  • Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

  • Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

  • Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

  • Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

  • Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

  • Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

  • Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

  • Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

Who you are

  • A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end.

  • Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration.

  • Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

  • Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

  • Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

  • Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday.

  • Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts.

  • Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams.

  • Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

Experience and background

  • Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several.

  • Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

  • Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis.

  • Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population.

  • Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes.

  • A track record of using analysis to influence decisions, not just to report on outcomes, in a role where you had some accountability for commercial results.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior stakeholders.

  • Experience with Open Banking data or cashflow underwriting is a plus, as is experience in a fast-growing fintech.

What we offer:

  • Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity

  • Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days per year

  • One month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership

  • Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

raw.title: Staff Engineer - Platform & Tooling
raw.description:
Who is Atominvest

Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows.

Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

About the role

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

 

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

 

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.

As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.

It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.

The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

  • Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

  • Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

  • Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

  • Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

  • Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

  • Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

  • Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

  • Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

  • Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

  • Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

  • At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

  • Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

  • Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

  • Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

You'll probably enjoy this if

  • You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

  • You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

  • You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team.

  • You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster.

  • You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

  • You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.

This probably isn't for you if

  • You want a pure DevOps or SRE role.

  • You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible.

What you'll bring

Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you.

  • Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda.

  • Infrastructure as code as a habit, with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

  • Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt.

  • Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's.

  • Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

  • Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb.

  • Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do.

  • Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple.

  • Tooling you've built for AI agents, not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.

How we hire

We want to see how you actually work, so there are no whiteboard puzzles.

  1. Screening call with me (20 minutes)

  2. Competencies interview with me (30 minutes)

  3. Technical deep dive with a few of our engineers (90 minutes)

  4. Culture fit interview with our CEO, Hemal (30 minutes)

I'll be your main point of contact throughout. You'll know what to expect before each stage, and if we don't make an offer, I'll give you feedback.

raw.description:
We're customer obsessed. We put the customer at the heart of everything we do - and we're looking for people who feel the same way.

About Bike Club

Bike Club is the easiest way to keep kids on the right sized bike. Through our subscription model, we remove the hassle of buying, outgrowing and reselling children's bikes, so families always have the right bike, right when they need it. We are a purpose led, fast-growing business built on ease, care, progress and joy - with a relentless focus on customer growth, retention and building a more circular approach to children's cycling.

Role Summary and Engagement

Bike Club is looking for a fractional Product Lead to lead the member product, turn customer needs and commercial priorities into a clear direction and a prioritised roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements. The role combines senior Product leadership with practical discovery and delivery coordination in a lean team.

The Product Lead will also establish an AI-enabled Product function, using AI to speed up customer insight, discovery, prototyping and experimentation. They will identify where AI and automation can improve the member experience or business efficiency, and turn the strongest opportunities into prioritised, measurable initiatives.

This is a part-time fixed-term employment or freelance contract estimated at 3 days per week for a period of 3 months.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product direction and roadmap: own the direction and roadmap across the member lifecycle: joining, managing a subscription, ongoing membership, exchange and retention. Balance member value with operational efficiency, cost and business priorities.

  • Discovery: lead discovery with members and colleagues across Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and markets. Use research, behavioural data and service insight to define problems before committing to solutions.

  • Lifecycle and retention: work jointly with Marketing and the retention owner on lifecycle journeys, retention initiatives, experiments and shared measures. Product owns the supporting experience and requirements. Marketing owns campaign and channel execution.

  • Requirements and backlog: turn agreed priorities into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Maintain one prioritised product backlog, including operational improvements and approved AI or automation initiatives.

  • Investment cases: build proportionate cases for investment, setting out expected benefits, cost, dependencies and how outcomes will be measured. Recommend stopping or deferring work where value is insufficient.

  • Delivery: agree delivery commitments with Engineering using realistic estimates and available capacity. Coordinate stakeholders, adoption and launches with the combined QA and Delivery role, keeping risks and changes visible.

  • Marketing autonomy: support Marketing with appropriate content, landing-page and experimentation capabilities. Agree the boundary between the member product, CRM and support tools.

  • AI in Product work: use AI routinely for research synthesis, analysis, requirements development, prototyping and experiment design, and validate findings against customer evidence.

  • Prioritise valuable applications with Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and the Data and Automation function. Test assumptions and build proportionate business cases. Customer-service automation should support the wider member journey.

  • Share responsibility with Marketing for using AI to support lifecycle insight, proposition testing and retention experiments, with agreed measures of customer and commercial impact.

  • Leave things in a better state: because the engagement is part-time and time-limited, document the roadmap, backlog, ways of working and AI approach so the team can continue without the Product Lead, and hand over clearly at the end.

Requirements

  • Extensive Product Management experience including owning a digital product roadmap and delivering measurable customer and commercial improvements, preferably in a subscription, membership or related consumer business.

  • Strong discovery skills, including customer interviews, journey mapping, data interpretation, problem definition and testing assumptions before investment.

  • Commercial judgement: can compare value, effort, cost and risk, build practical investment cases and make clear prioritisation decisions.

  • Ability to lead across functions, challenge senior stakeholders constructively and maintain focus when priorities compete.

  • Experience working with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Customer Service and Operations through delivery, launch and continuous improvement.

  • Demonstrable experience embedding AI into Product workflows, with examples of faster learning, better decisions or reduced effort. Able to distinguish valuable AI applications from features that add unnecessary complexity.

  • Track record of working independently and effectively in a part-time, fractional or interim capacity, making visible progress in limited days a week.

  • Able to start quickly, and leave behind clear documentation and repeatable ways of working.

Measures Of Success

Baselines, numerical targets, data sources and review dates are agreed with the executive sponsor and relevant business owners within the first 30 days. Delivery and outcomes are reviewed weekly.

  • Member retention: improvement in the agreed retention or cancellation measure for targeted journeys, assessed jointly with Marketing and the retention owner.

  • Member experience: improvement in self-service completion and reduction in avoidable support contact for prioritised journeys, without deterioration in customer experience.

  • Conversion: improvement in agreed joining and exchange conversion measures, using experiments or comparable cohorts where practical.

  • Speed of learning: reduced time from identifying a customer problem to testing a solution, with evidence that decisions remain grounded in customer insight.

  • AI and automation: validated initiatives deliver agreed improvements in member experience, retention or operational efficiency, measured with the relevant business owner.

  • Roadmap value: proportion of priority initiatives with a stated outcome, baseline and measurement plan before delivery, followed by a documented benefits review.

  • Delivery confidence: performance against jointly agreed milestones, with changes in scope, priorities and dependencies recorded and communicated early.

Our Values

We look for people who live our values every day:

Ease: we make things simple for our members and for each other.

Care: we look after our customers, our colleagues and our bikes.

Progress: we keep improving, learning and raising the bar.

Joy: we help kids fall in love with cycling, and enjoy the work we do.

Why Bike Club?

You'll be joining a business with a clear purpose, a genuinely different proposition and significant opportunity to grow.

This is a rare opportunity to build the operating system for our national refurbishment and distribution site from the ground up, shaping how Bike Club gets the right bike to every family, right when they need it.

raw.title: Enforcement Appeals Specialist
raw.description:
Introduction to Role & Team

Bumble Inc. is looking for an Enforcement Appeals Specialist to join our Trust Operations team. We are seeking a highly motivated, hands-on candidate who thrives in a cross-functional environment and is excited to support the evolution of our Trust Operations team.

In this position, you will investigate and respond to members' appeals as a result of account restrictions and content moderation. You will help uphold Bumble Inc.’s Community Guidelines by reviewing and enforcing actions on violating accounts and content to maintain a safe and respectful environment. The ideal candidate is comfortable working with sensitive content, including child exploitation, graphic or physical sexual violence, suicide and self-harm, and other potentially distressing material.

Trust and safety are embedded in Bumble Inc.’s mission of creating a world where all relationships are healthy and equitable. Our wider Trust organization includes centralized and dedicated teams focused on:

  • Creating products and systems that proactively detect and prevent harm and promote healthy, kind relationships.

  • Developing policies that govern and adjudicate responsible, safe, inclusive, and respectful behaviour and content across all Bumble Inc. platforms.

  • Supporting members who experience safety incidents in a trauma-informed, empathetic manner.

This role will be based in London, UK reporting to the Enforcement Appeals Manager.

Please note: This position involves exposure to sensitive and graphic content, including but not limited to vulgar, violent, and sexual content.

What You’ll Do

  • Review and take action on members’ appeals for content removals, account bans, or other enforcement actions in a timely and accurate manner.

  • Provide high-touch, trauma-informed safety support to members who have experienced safety incidents.

  • Collaborate with internal teams, including Trust & Safety, Customer Experience, and Legal, to escalate and resolve complex safety cases.

  • Help enforce Bumble Inc.’s policies by reviewing and processing accounts and content flagged for safety violations.

  • Participate in on-call rotations, including nights, weekends, and holidays, as needed.

About You

  • Have 2–4 years of experience in a Trust & Safety, customer support, crisis response, or content moderation role, preferably in a high-risk or safety-focused environment.

  • Have demonstrated ability to work with sensitive content and provide support in cases involving child exploitation, sexual violence, and self-harm.

  • Have experience handling high-touch safety escalations, particularly those involving vulnerable individuals.

  • Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide clear, empathetic, and professional responses.

  • Have experience collaborating with Business Process Outsourcers (BPOs) to ensure quality and consistency in safety-related workflows (preferred).

  • Are able to work independently, prioritize urgent tasks, and make sound judgment calls under pressure.

  • Have proficiency in Spanish, Portuguese, French, or another second language (preferred).

  • Are passionate about Bumble’s mission and values.

  • Are empathetic, resilient, and comfortable working in emotionally challenging situations.

  • Have a strong understanding of online safety issues and best practices in Trust & Safety.

  • Are detail-oriented and able to balance efficiency with thoughtful decision-making.

  • Are comfortable working flexible hours to support global teams and participating in on-call shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Benefits & Perks

  • Annual personal learning & development budget

  • Private Medical Insurance (PMI)

  • Private Dental Insurance

  • Babylon Health app

  • Mental health support

  • Enhanced parental leave, including a highly competitive maternity package

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Subsidised gym membership

  • ‘Double matched’ pension contributions up to 6%

  • Premium App Access

About Us

Bumble Inc. is the parent company of Bumble Date, BFF, and Badoo. The Bumble platform enables people to build healthy and equitable relationships, through Kind Connections. Founded by Whitney Wolfe Herd in 2014, Bumble was one of the first dating apps built with women at the center and connects people across dating (Bumble Date) and friendship (BFF). BFF is a friendship app where people in all stages of life can meet people nearby and create meaningful platonic connections and community based on shared interests. Badoo, which was founded in 2006, is one of the pioneers of web and mobile dating products.

AI Fluency

AI is important to us. We’re excited by people who are curious and experimental, and who think thoughtfully about how AI can amplify their impact and outcomes.

We encourage you to use AI responsibly as you prepare your application. Please don’t use it to fabricate experiences or answer questions live in interviews. We care deeply about authenticity and want to understand your real skills, judgment and voice, because building a meaningful, genuine connection with you matters to us.

Final Compensation

Will be determined based on factors such as the selected candidate’s qualifications, relevant experience, skill set, and other job-related considerations.

Inclusion at Bumble Inc.

Bumble Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage people of all ages, color, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer and non-binary people, veterans, parents, people with disabilities, and neurodivergent people to apply. We're happy to make any reasonable adjustments that will help you feel more confident throughout the process, please don't hesitate to let us know how we can help.

In your application, please feel free to note which pronouns you use (For example: she/her, he/him, they/them, etc).

AI in Bumble Inc. Hiring

At Bumble, we may use AI tools to support parts of our recruitment process — such as helping us record, transcribe, and summarize conversations, and supporting job alignment by comparing resumes and job descriptions to highlight skills and potential roles that may be a good match. These tools help us work more efficiently and stay focused on you during our conversations. Importantly, all hiring decisions are made by people. AI is used only to support our team’s efficiency and improve the candidate experience — not to evaluate or decide on your candidacy. Participation in AI-supported interviews and conversations is completely voluntary and will not impact your candidacy. If you’d prefer to opt out, simply let your recruiter or interviewer know at the start of a call, or anytime during the interview or conversation. Summaries and related data are retained only as long as needed in line with our internal data retention policies. If at any point you’d like a transcription or summary deleted, please contact your recruiter directly.

Fraudulent Candidate Detection

Our applicant tracking system analyzes signals relating to device, IP, email, and phone data associated with each application to protect applicants and our hiring process from fraudulent applications. These signals provide indicators for internal review only and do not constitute a definitive determination of identity or intent. No applicant is rejected, advanced, or otherwise affected based solely on this analysis without human review

For further information on how we hold and manage your data, please refer to our Privacy Policy.

raw.title: Deployment Strategist SAP & ERP Specialist
raw.description:
TL;DR

You know how to walk into an enterprise, spot the pain points in its ERP processes, and see what good could look like. At Conduct you turn that into a game changing moment: you show leadership, with confidence, how Conduct will transform the way they run SAP. You own optimising the delivery of transformation projects with Conduct, from the first use case to adoption across the business. You build the trust that turns a pilot into a long-term partnership, and the product insights you bring back directly shape what we build next.

Why Conduct

The world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the systems they run on. Today they don't, and you've seen why firsthand.

Every new product line, pricing change or process redesign runs into SAP estates layered with decades of custom code, user exits and enhancements no single person fully understands. Requirements take months to ship. S/4HANA migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain, and the 2027 ECC deadline is forcing every large enterprise to face it.

We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems. We've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service.

We're a small, talent-dense team doing our life's work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world's largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out.

What you'll own

You will make sure Conduct lands and sticks inside our most strategic SAP customers. You join accounts early, shape how Conduct fits into their transformation programmes, and fully take over post-sale. You'll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what ships in the product.

  • Be the SAP brain in the room. Translate between CIOs, process owners, Basis teams and our engineers. Scope use cases across finance, supply chain, procurement and sales that land real value fast.

  • Design the transformation. Get under the skin of complex, heavily customised ECC and S/4HANA landscapes. Conceptualise where Conduct can have the biggest impact, then lead the deployment that gets the customer there.

  • Turn pilots into partnerships. Onboard hundreds of end users, prove ROI, spot expansion signals and hold the early commercial conversations that grow an account.

  • Shape the product. You'll have a direct line into product and engineering. Your view of how SAP actually runs in the real world will shape our roadmap.

  • Build the engine. Our GTM team is small and lean. You'll build the onboarding flows, tooling and reusable playbooks that let customer capacity compound without headcount growing linearly.

  • Work with our SI partners. You speak their language. Help partners deploy Conduct inside their own programmes.

No two days look the same. You'll fly out to customers when it counts and spend the rest of the time building alongside the team.

Who we hire

We're looking for people obsessed with delivering for customers. You'll fit right in if former colleagues would, without hesitating, call you one of the sharpest people they've worked with.

In practice that tends to look like:

  • 3+ years in SAP or ERP consulting, at a Big Four firm, a global SI or a specialist SAP partner. You've been on live implementations, rollouts or S/4HANA transformations, not just advisory.

  • Real depth in at least one area of SAP. Functional (FI/CO, SD, MM, PP, EWM), technical (ABAP, integration, BTP) or solution architecture. You understand how processes and custom code fit together across the landscape.

  • Client-facing confidence. You've run workshops, owned a workstream and earned the trust of senior stakeholders who were sceptical at first.

  • Commercial instinct. You notice the next problem worth solving, and you understand that a great deployment is how accounts grow.

  • Builder energy. You want to do the hands-on customer work and build the process behind it. Ambiguity excites you more than it worries you.

  • Curiosity about AI. You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to want to learn how it works and where it breaks.

  • Low ego, high self-awareness. You're comfortable saying "I don't know" in a complex technical room, then going and figuring it out.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We care more about trajectory and sharpness than a perfect match.

Endpoint & Device Management

Service Delivery & Support

Asset Lifecycle & Vendor Management

Enablement

Required Qualifications

raw.title: Head of Salesforce and Client Engagement Platforms
raw.description:
Who we are

Flagstone is one of Europe's leading cash deposit marketplaces. Our clients open one account and gain access to 400+ deposit accounts from 70+ banks and building societies. Our clients span individuals, business leaders, charities, entrepreneurs, and guardians of family wealth.

We've been profitable for three consecutive years. In March 2024 we secured a £108 million investment from Estancia Capital Partners, bringing total funding raised to £150 million alongside OMERS Ventures and Kindred Capital. We're now around 400 people.

Our strategy is to broaden our client base across upper-affluent individuals and UK SMEs, extend our product line, and establish Flagstone as a well-known direct-to-consumer brand.

The Role

We are looking for a senior, commercially minded Head of Salesforce & Client Engagement Platforms to own and design the platforms that power our CRM, client service, and engagement capabilities. Salesforce is one of our most strategic platforms, and teams across the business rely on it to hit their goals. A big part of this role is working with our executive and senior leadership teams to balance competing priorities, make clear calls on what matters most, and set the direction for where our platforms go next.

You will turn the strategies set by our business leaders, including our CRM strategy, into platform capabilities that help our commercial and service teams succeed.

Our core platform is Salesforce, supplemented by best-of-breed support, telephony, communication, and engagement tools. We choose the right tool for each job rather than relying on a single vendor.

There's a big opportunity ahead. We want to build a real-time, 360 view of every client, so we can give them timely, relevant information across email, SMS and our other channels. Getting there is complex, covering vendors, architecture, data and design, and this role will own the long-term view of how we get there, with AI at the centre.

You will lead a multidisciplinary team, with a strong focus on AI and agent-based automation. In your first year, you'll set a clear multi-year roadmap, earn the trust of leaders across the business, and deliver measurable gains through AI and automation.

What you'll own

Stakeholder Leadership & Prioritisation: Build trusted relationships with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Operations, Client Services, Product, and CRM and Digital, including members of our executive and operating committees. Balance competing requests, agree delivery priorities with senior leadership, and hold a clear line on what gets done and why.

Strategy & Roadmap: Shape the long-term platform strategy, roadmap, and performance metrics for Salesforce and the wider CRM, client service, and engagement stack, working in close partnership with our technology leadership. Make build, buy, or integrate decisions in line with business strategy.

Platform Architecture & Design: Act as the design authority for Salesforce and the wider engagement stack. Own the target architecture, org strategy, data model, and security model, and set the design standards and best practices that the team and delivery partners follow, including environment strategy, DevOps, and release management. Review and approve significant solution designs so the platform scales, performs, and stays easy to maintain.

Client Service & Engagement: Own our client service and engagement tools, including telephony and chat channels, and AI-led support platforms, and make sure they work with the CRM to give clients a consistent experience.

Platform Governance: Build and enforce a governance framework to prioritise change requests, manage technical debt, keep the platform stable, and ensure data security, data quality, and compliance with GDPR and our regulatory obligations, including Consumer Duty.

Data & Integration: Own the integration architecture so client data flows reliably between Salesforce, our support tools, and our core systems, giving teams a single view of the client.

Vendor & Budget Management: Own the platform budget and manage vendor relationships, contracts, and performance, including third-party risk oversight.

Team Leadership: Lead and develop a team of architects, developers, administrators, configuration experts, and automation and AI specialists.

Value Realisation: Report on platform performance, user adoption, return on investment, and roadmap milestones to the C-suite.

AI Transformation: Define and deliver AI-enabled platform capabilities, including agent-based automation, across our CRM, service, and engagement technology.

What you'll bring

Senior Stakeholder Management: A track record of building trust with the C-suite and senior leaders, balancing competing priorities across the business, and challenging requirements constructively. You're comfortable holding your ground and bringing technical and commercial teams together around a shared direction.

Experience: Significant experience designing, owning, or leading enterprise-scale Salesforce platforms in a commercial or tech-enabled business.

Architecture & Platform Design: Experience designing and setting up enterprise Salesforce orgs, including data and security models, integration patterns, multi-cloud architecture, and environment and release management. A clear view of what good looks like on Salesforce, with a track record of setting design standards and best practice, and of fixing platforms that were poorly designed.

Strategic Track Record: Proven success in defining and delivering a multi-year platform strategy and roadmap for CRM, service, or engagement technology, with measurable business outcomes.

Functional Depth: Deep knowledge of Salesforce across multiple clouds, and experience with other CRM and customer service platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot, and Zendesk. Experience with AI-led CX tools such as Lorikeet is a strong advantage.

AI & Automation: Experience delivering AI and agent-based automation in customer service or engagement settings, including the controls needed to protect customer outcomes.

Commercial & Service Acumen: Strong grasp of commercial and client workflows, such as partner and pipeline management, onboarding, retention, and service journeys, and how platform choices, including telephony, affect agent productivity and customer outcomes.

Leadership & Governance: Proven experience managing internal technical teams, vendors, budgets, and change programmes in an agile environment.

How we reward you:

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

  • Hybrid working - Spend at least 1 day a week with your team in our collaborative London office

  • Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance

  • Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.

  • A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.

  • Around the World scheme - 3 months work from anywhere scheme

  • Mental wellbeing support – Access therapy and mental health sessions through Spill

  • Learning and development – £1,000 personal development budget to help you grow in your role.

  • Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded

  • Medical cash plan - To help you with the costs of dental and optical expenses

  • Life insurance and Income Protection- four times your annual salary for peace of mind

  • Matched pension contributions up to 5%

  • 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days

  • Enhanced Parental Leave – enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.

All are welcome.

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

raw.title: Manager: Compliance Advisory (and Data Protection)
raw.description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

The opportunity

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end.

As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it.

What success looks like

In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand.

To do this you'll be involved in:

Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time)

  • Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.

  • Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.

  • Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.

  • Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.

  • Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.

  • Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

  • Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

  • Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.

Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed)

Being our DPO means:

  • advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)

  • monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies

  • training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection

  • being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

In your first year, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. And you’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

  • Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.
