  • Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

  • Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In Germany, home to the largest electricity market in Europe and a roadmap toward Net Zero by 2045, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. We are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As we expand our footprint in Germany and the wider European market, we are looking for a Senior Client Delivery Lead to support our German GenerationFlex clients on their Kraken onboarding journey and wider business transformation.

🐙 About GenerationFlex

The energy system is changing fast. Renewables are growing, demand is becoming more peaky, and grid constraints are showing up in more places, more often. Kraken GenerationFlex is how utilities and asset owners navigate that complexity at scale.

We help organisations run portfolios of grid-scale assets - BESS, renewables, and co-located sites - in a way that's commercially aligned, operationally safe, and practical to manage day to day.

From trading enablement and control & dispatch, to alerts, data services, and settlements, our platform gives teams the visibility and automation they need to respond well to change across multiple assets, markets, and regulations.

We're a mission-driven team making the big green dent in the world, and we're looking for people ready to help shape what that looks like next.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in: The Delivery Team

We are looking for an experienced Client Delivery Lead to build industry-leading product experiences for our European clients. If you love making things better for clients, building great products, working with technology (software + hardware), bringing people together to find solutions, then you’ve come to the right place.

GenerationFlex is different to the wider Kraken universe and highly cross-functional: our product bridges software and hardware in order to allow our clients’ trading teams to effectively control their assets across multiple markets and asset types. The Client Delivery Lead has direct responsibility for creating, managing and prioritising the client onboarding roadmap to ensure clarity and understanding with both the Kraken and client business. They need to always work in partnership with the product, software engineering, asset onboarding and electrical engineering teams at Kraken and are the main point of contact for our clients and their partners.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Client relationship: manage and coordinate a multitude of stakeholders during the initial client implementation phase, ranging from construction site managers to software engineers to senior business stakeholders. Be the first point of contact for tech development and issue resolution during the implementation phase, organise workstreams, flag dependencies, coordinate internal and external teams, and provide clear and concise updates to keep everyone on track and on the same page.

  • Regional Market Expertise: act as the subject matter expert for our clients and wider Kraken teams thanks to your deep understanding of the German and European energy markets, including hardware and connectivity requirements, TSOs and DSOs, re-dispatch, ancillary-service requirements and competitor landscape. Help evaluate hardware and software solutions for regional fit.

  • Kraken technology: Develop deep product knowledge of Kraken’s technology offering in European markets, and, together with your regional market expertise, help our clients along a smooth onboarding journey. Understand our clients’ user needs and how our capabilities enable their asset management and energy trading strategies.

  • Strategic outlook: work closely with our account managers to understand our clients’ priorities and enable strategic business reviews and client transformation workshops. Spot opportunities for product enhancements, market expansion, user growth and upselling.

  • Internal process improvements: drive internal process improvements to enhance our onboarding journey and speed up time to value. Work closely with product, engineering, customer success and support teams to provide a smooth client experience.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • In this position you will be laser focused on satisfying our client’s needs.

  • We are looking for people with strong problem solving skills and a super positive solutions oriented mindset. If you have a taste for raising up to challenges and a winning mindset, this position is the right fit for you!

  • Strong client delivery and/or product ownership experience working across software and hardware.

  • Experience of working with complex delivery pipelines for clients, coordinating multiple teams, spotting dependencies, mitigating risks and maintaining momentum.

  • Exceptional relationship management across a wide range of stakeholders internally and externally: software engineers & architects, electrical engineers, C-level executives, commercial teams, project managers, product managers, cyber security experts, procurement & logistics, finance etc.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to take a complicated technical problem and clearly explain the issue, impact, owner and next action. Ability to communicate at high-level and low-level.

  • Strong influencing skills and ability to challenge traditional ways of thinking.

  • Strong interest in understanding the intricacies of energy markets. Experience working with flexibility products is a plus.

  • Solid understanding of technology and associated trends. Agile delivery experience and understanding of APIs, data flows, system integrations and cloud software architecture.

  • Patience and initiative - our clients are undergoing huge transformations that take time and require our understanding

  • Time management and a get-stuff-done attitude.

  • Native or professional fluency in English. Other European languages are a plus.

  • Occasional travel is required as part of this role.

 

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Fluency in other (human) languages.

  • In-depth knowledge of the energy market in Europe, e.g. market players, trading practices, regulations, compliance.

  • Experience in flexible generation, battery storage, renewable energy, demand response or distributed energy resources. Commissioning or integrating generators, BESS, solar, EV infrastructure or other industrial energy assets.

  • A working understanding of industrial gateways, edge devices, IoT connectivity, and industrial communication protocols and controlled environments (e.g. Modbus, OPC UA).

Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🏡 Where you'll fit in

You'll own strategic technology negotiations end to end. That covers tier-1 SaaS, outsourcing, and core billing platform deals for regulated utilities and energy retailers. You'll report to the Chief Commercial Officer and carry board-level accountability for deals above $100m.

You'll lead a cross-functional deal team and make sure every seat is filled by the right person:

  • Executive sponsor and deal owner: holds the mandate and budget, and breaks deadlocks fast.

  • Lead negotiator: runs the table, controls pacing and concessions, and stays separate from the delivery owner. This is the seat you'll usually hold.

  • Commercial and pricing lead: builds the should-cost model and covers pricing structures, benchmarking, and total cost of ownership (TCO).

  • Legal and contracts counsel: covers liability caps, intellectual property (IP) ownership, indemnities, termination, data protection, and step-in rights.

  • Technical and solution architect: tests feasibility, scope, service levels (SLAs), and integration and security claims.

  • Operations and service owner: brings realistic requirements, transition plans, and governance from the business.

  • Finance and procurement: covers payment terms, currency and indexation, and audit and benchmarking rights.

  • Risk, security, and compliance: handles regulatory, data residency, and resilience requirements.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Lead negotiation of multi-year technology and outsourcing agreements worth $250m to $1bn+ in total contract value, from selection through signature.

  • Set the commercial playbook: pricing structures, walk-away positions, a concession log, and fallback positions on liability, service levels, and exit.

  • Agree one position before you sit down. Rank priorities as must-have, trade, or give, and define your walk-away point (your best alternative to a negotiated agreement, or BATNA).

  • Structure deals that fit the risk: fixed price, time and materials, outcome-based, and gain-share, with volume bands, rate cards, indexation, and price-down glide paths.

  • Decide which risks to transfer, share, or keep, and put a price on each one.

  • Negotiate core billing and Customer Information System (CIS) replacements, including migration plans, regulatory change, service levels, and exit terms.

  • Define scope precisely: baseline, assumptions, dependencies, and exclusions. Most disputes start here, so you'll settle them before signature.

  • Plan the exit from day one: lock-in, data portability, step-in rights, and termination assistance.

  • Build competitive tension, keep alternatives alive, and manage timing, such as a vendor's quarter-end.

  • Bring Delivery and Operations into the deal early, so the contract works in practice.

  • Lock in key-personnel clauses, so the vendor's A-team doesn't sell while the B-team delivers.

  • Set up governance, benchmarking, and audit rights that keep working after signature, and track change requests, renewals, and exit costs alongside the headline price.

  • Recruit and grow the team: energy-billing experts, a migration lead, SaaS counsel, and regulatory specialists, with a clear capability model and a RACI (who's responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed).

  • Coach executive sponsors on leverage and timing, and run negotiation war-gaming before the big moments.

  • Step in early when a deal or migration drifts, and reset milestones, scope, and commercials to get it back on track.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

Experience

  • Ideally 20+ years negotiating multi-year technology and outsourcing agreements for regulated utilities or energy retailers.

  • A track record on 15+ transactions of $250m to $1bn+ total contract value, including core billing or CIS replacement, cloud migration, or managed services.

  • Energy domain knowledge: meter-to-cash, tariffs, market codes, and regulatory billing obligations.

  • The credibility to work with boards, CFOs, and regulators, and to say no when a deal doesn't add up.

Capabilities

  • Commercial acumen. You understand vendor economics and margin levers, and you know where suppliers make their money (change requests and renewals, for example).

  • Deal structuring. You choose between fixed price, time and materials, outcome-based, and gain-share, and you set volume bands and price-down paths that hold up over 3 to 7 years.

  • Risk allocation judgment. You know which risks to transfer, share, or keep, and you can price them.

  • Technical depth. You can challenge a vendor's assumptions on scope, effort, and architecture.

  • Scope and requirements clarity. You define what's in, what's out, and what has to be true for the price to hold.

  • Exit and transition planning. You cover lock-in, data portability, step-in, and termination assistance from the start.

  • Commercial modeling. You build multi-year margin, cash flow, cost-to-serve, and should-cost models.

How you work

  • You bring one voice to the table. No side deals, and every concession goes in the log.

  • You build leverage with a competitive process, and you keep your composure when a vendor pushes a deadline or a "sign now for a discount" offer.

  • You push hard on terms and protect the long-term partnership, because we'll live with the deal for years.

  • You work well across cultures and time zones, including with vendors based in other markets.

  • You bring legal, commercial, and technical colleagues into one room instead of letting them negotiate in silos.

⭐ Bonus points

  • Time spent on the supplier side, so you know how vendor economics and margin levers work from the inside.

  • A legal or contracts background.

  • Negotiation or value-selling certifications, such as Harvard PON.

  • Working knowledge of Ofgem licence conditions, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and operational resilience rules such as the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

  • A degree in business, engineering, law, or a related field.

raw.description:
What we are building

Mimica is an AI-powered process intelligence platform enabling enterprises and individuals to reclaim their most precious resource: time. We've all seen repetitive tasks and redundant processes quietly drain productivity and creativity. Not because companies don’t want to become more efficient, but because they don’t know where to start.

Our team

Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI.

Our approach to engineering

  • We prioritize customer needs first

  • We work in small, project-based teams

  • We have flexibility in terms of the problems we work on

  • We own the full lifecycle of our projects

  • We avoid silos and encourage taking up tasks in new areas

  • We balance quality and velocity

  • We have a shared responsibility for our production code

  • We each set our own routine to maximize our productivity

 

Your mission

 

You’ll join us as a Machine Learning Engineer/ Data Scientist for Mimica’s Data Intelligence team, whose goal is to transform raw recorded data into clean, structured, anonymized data that powers the work of other teams.

You’ll own key parts of our ML pipelines end to end, making them more accurate, cost-efficient, and trustworthy. Along the way, you’ll build evaluations and LLM judges, run experiments, and transform promising results into validated production improvements.

Your work will be applied and LLM-heavy, with opportunities to evaluate and fine-tune open-source models and build smaller, task-specific models.

If you enjoy taking ML beyond experiments, this is your chance to shape the systems at the heart of Mimica’s products and see your work deliver value to real users at scale.

 

Part of your day-to-day

 

  • Own, debug, and improve production pipelines for accuracy and efficiency.

  • Design, build, and iterate on LLM evals and LLM-as-a-judge systems, including the datasets, metrics, and benchmarks to monitor quality.

  • Run rigorous experiments on prompts, pipeline design, model choice, and inputs (e.g., OCR text vs. image + OCR), and turn the results into clear recommendations.

  • Drive LLM efficiency improvements across our pipelines by comparing models, restructuring steps, and replacing LLM calls with smaller, purpose-built models where it makes sense.

  • Expand our anonymization pipeline, including evaluating and adapting existing models.

  • Work with Python and quality engineers to take experiments into production, and share responsibility for the code you ship.

  • Document findings in writing (eg. experiment reports, design docs)

 

What we’re looking for

 

Primarily, we’re looking for an individual with an experiment- and data-driven researcher mindset with good coding habits. This includes:

  • Solid machine learning/data science background: you understand experimental design, data splits, metrics, bias, and statistical significance, and you know when a result is real.

  • Hands-on experience applying LLMs in production or near-production settings, especially evaluating them: building eval sets, LLM judges and benchmarks, and iterating on prompts and pipelines against them.

  • Comfortable getting deep into messy data: exploring it, troubleshooting issues, and transforming insights into measurable improvements.

  • Strong Python and good engineering skills. You write clear, readable, tested code that others can take to production, even if you’re not the one owning the infrastructure.

  • Able to work independently on ambiguous problems: framing the question, choosing the approach, and deciding on the acceptance criteria to ship.

  • Communicate clearly in spoken and written English, including explaining technical trade-offs to both technical and non-technical audiences

 

Bonus / Nice to have

  • Experience with classical ML or deep learning model development.

  • Experience with image/OCR pipelines or face-related anonymization

  • Experience shipping end-to-end ML features in a startup or scale-up environment.

 

Location

This is a fully remote position. To make sure we work well together, we’re only considering candidates based in the UK or Europe, in time zones compatible with London (typically UTC-1 to UTC+3).

We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.

Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.

Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.

Internal communications at Multiverse isn't a downstream function. It's a strategic one.

That means shaping All Hands, advising the exec team, translating data into narratives people can actually repeat, and building the rhythms that keep colleagues informed week to week — not just when something big happens.

We operate in a fast-moving space with real external scrutiny. You'll need to be a strong instinctive writer, calm under pressure, and confident enough to tell leadership what needs to be said and when. If you want to own the internal narrative of one of the most ambitious companies in the UK skills and AI space — this is the role.

Specifically, you will

raw.description:
About us

People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. In reality, hundred of thousands of operators acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on, with tools that have barely changed in decades and spending hours a day on email. Nexcade is building the agentic operating system for those people, transforming the way people communicate and optimise the $1T spend on logistics every year.

Our agents are live in production with leading global Freight Forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are rapidly expanding the platform to touch every part of the logistics lifecycle.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality from top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

How we work

  • Everybody builds, founders included. The whole company is technical and runs on coding agents. You will not be asked to write production software, but you will use agents for discovery synthesis, specs, prototypes and data analysis rather than doing them by hand.

  • Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

  • At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

  • End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

  • In person, in London. We value synchronous communication.

  • Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

  • Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

The role

We’re building the AI platform freight forwarders rely on. We started with quoting and are expanding across the shipment lifecycle. As Product Lead, you will be central to that expansion, helping decide where we focus and turning those decisions into products customers depend on.

What you’ll do:

  • Own product outcomes: Own the roadmap, priorities and performance of specific products, from defining the customer problem through launch, rollout and adoption. Partner with the founders on overall product direction and strategy.

  • Build from customer insight: Work closely with freight forwarders across commercial and operational roles. Understand how they work, identify the problems customers share and build products for those needs rather than one-off solutions.

  • Prototype and build: Turn ideas into working prototypes and early product versions, using AI tools and code to test them with customers. Work hands-on with engineering to take promising ideas into production, not just write specs and hand them over.

  • Drive product expansion: Build a clear view of the market, including where we win, where we do not compete and why customers choose us. Use that understanding to identify the next workflows Nexcade should enter and turn them into products that grow revenue.

  • Raise the standard of product thinking: Define success measures, test assumptions and examine accuracy, edge cases and second-order effects before scaling. Write clear specs and decision documents, including a written recommendation on the hard calls.

  • Build the product operating system: Establish a clear planning and decision-making cadence without adding bureaucracy. Make sure product meetings are well prepared, teams have the context they need and decisions translate into shipped work.

  • Make product and platform trade-offs: Work closely with engineering to decide when to invest in shared capabilities and when a faster, product-specific approach is right.

What we look for

  • Strong product judgement: You have owned meaningful product work in a complex B2B product and can show how your decisions changed customer behaviour or business results. You define success clearly and test assumptions, accuracy and edge cases before scaling.

  • Product taste: You can turn complex workflows into products that feel simple, coherent and trustworthy. You care about the details that make people choose to use them.

  • Technical fluency: You work effectively with strong engineers, understand trade-offs across architecture, AI, data and integrations and bring the customer and product perspective to choices about speed, quality and reuse.

  • Excellent judgement: You get beyond what customers ask for to understand how their work really happens and distinguish repeatable needs from bespoke requests. You use customer and market insight to make product choices that drive adoption, expansion and revenue.

  • High agency and directness: You take ownership, hold a high bar and disagree openly and constructively. You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast iteration and changing priorities.

  • Obsess over the problem: You are drawn to complex, messy problems in industries the economy depends on and want to understand how the people and systems behind them really work. Industry experience is a bonus, but not required.

Why join

The biggest product choices are still ahead: how deep we go, where we expand and how everything fits together. Our product is already live with leading freight forwarders and this role will shape what comes next. You will build AI for the work that keeps global trade moving, alongside a team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will get meaningful equity in the company you help build.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

🚀 Join the team transforming how real estate is transacted with AI

Orbital is building the first AI platform purpose-built for real estate transactions. With $60m Series B funding and a rapidly expanding our US and UK customer base serving some of the most prestigious law firms, including across the AmLaw rankings, as well as in-house real estate teams, title companies, and other organisations involved in the transaction.

🌟 The Opportunity

As our Customer Success Associate (Support), you will be the first point of contact for our customers, ensuring they get fast, expert answers and a seamless experience every day.

This role is built for someone at the start of their career who is smart, fast, and hungry to grow. You will:

  • Be the face of Orbital to our customers on a daily basis

  • Own support channels and become deeply expert in our product

  • Work alongside a Senior CSM across some of the most prestigious real estate legal practices and organisations in the US and UK.

  • Build the communication instincts and commercial acumen to progress toward full account ownership

This is a high-learning, high-exposure role with a direct path into Customer Success. Progression at Orbital can be vertical - into CSM and portfolio ownership — or diagonal into other high-growth functions as we scale.

🧠 What You’ll Do

  • Manage the inbound support queue and own first response- speed and quality are both very important here

  • Resolve customer queries accurately and promptly, escalating where needed

  • Build deep product fluency and become an internal product expert

  • Spot patterns and share structured feedback with Product and Engineering

  • Be comfortable picking up the phone, not every problem gets solved over email

Support Customer Adoption and Delivery

  • Assist with onboarding sessions, training materials, and customer rollout initiatives

  • Join client visits and build genuine familiarity with how our customers work — from law firm real estate practices to in-house legal teams and other participants in the transaction

Develop Commercial and Domain Expertise

  • Learn how SaaS renewals and expansions are run by sitting alongside a Senior CSM

  • Observe and, over time, participate in executive-level conversations with senior legal stakeholders

  • Build understanding of the real estate transaction lifecycle and how AI is transforming it

Help Build and Scale the CS Function

  • Contribute to scaled customer programmes — think webinars, user groups, product update communications, and onboarding initiatives designed to reach customers at volume

  • Support customer events — from in-person roundtables with law firm partners to virtual deep-dives with in-house real estate teams — helping coordinate logistics, materials, and follow-through

  • Use best-in-class AI tools creatively and intelligently — whether to draft customer communications, surface product insights, prepare briefing notes, or find smarter ways to do the work

  • Help shape the playbooks, processes, and norms we're building from scratch — your ideas about how we do things will actually get heard and implemented

  • Act as the connective tissue between our customers and Orbital’s Product, Engineering, and CS teams — making sure nothing falls through the cracks as we grow

✨ Who We’re Looking For

We are open to a range of backgrounds. The common thread is: bright, proactive, and genuinely interested in real estate and AI.

One of the following: Early-Career SaaS, Hypergrowth Tech or Real Estate Background

  • If you’ve spent 1–2 years as a BDR, SDR, or junior CS hire at a hypergrowth SaaS or AI company and you’ve genuinely stood out we want to hear from you.

  • 1–2 years of experience in a real estate-adjacent role whether in law, brokerage, transaction support, or CRE services. You understand how real estate deals work, you've handled complex documents, and you're used to operating in environments where the stakes are high and the people are demanding.

  • Commercial real estate paralegal (property, title, or transactional)

  • Research associate or operations coordinator in a CRE or legal environment

  • Any role where you've worked closely with real estate attorneys or on real estate due diligence

In All Cases, You Will Have:

  • Exceptional written communication — clear, professional, and precise

  • Fast response instincts — you treat a customer query as something to solve today, not tomorrow

  • Confidence picking up the phone and speaking with senior professionals

  • Intellectual curiosity — especially around AI (with evidenced usage) technology, and legal / real estate industries

  • High ownership mentality — you don't wait to be told

  • Comfort and credibility engaging with senior legal or real estate stakeholders

Ambition to grow — you want to own accounts, not just support them

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

raw.title: Data Engineering Lead
raw.description:
About Plasma

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.


The Team & Our Story

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

The Role

We're looking for a hands-on Data Lead to build Plasma's data function from the ground up. You'll be our first dedicated data hire, working across Consumer, Payments and Business to give the company one trusted view of its users, its money and its operations.

At first you'll build much of the platform yourself: our Snowflake warehouse, the pipelines that feed it and the modelled layer on top. As the function grows, you'll choose the tools, set the standards and hire the team.

The Work

  • Own Plasma's data platform end to end: the Snowflake warehouse, ingestion from production systems and third-party providers, and the modelled layer the rest of the company builds on

  • Define the metrics the company runs on, including funded users, activation, engagement, balances, spend and retention, and make sure every team uses the same definitions

  • Partner with Consumer to understand how users behave across regions, segments and products, and turn that into specific product decisions

  • Design and analyse experiments, and be clear about when a result is real and when it isn't

  • Work with Payments and finance so the business can trust its numbers: reconciliation across ledgers, providers and banking partners, revenue reporting and unit economics

  • Find fraudulent and abusive patterns across onboarding, funding, card spend and transfers, and build the signals and rules that let risk and operations act on them

  • Treat data quality, testing, access control and PII handling as part of the platform, not an afterthought

  • Choose tools deliberately, set standards for the function and hire the team as Plasma scales

The Bar

  • A senior, hands-on data practitioner with a track record of both building a data platform and using it

  • Deep SQL and data modelling skills, with enough engineering range to build and run production pipelines yourself

  • Comfortable starting from very little, and building something that still makes sense when the team is five times bigger

  • Strong judgment on tradeoffs: speed vs. rigour, build vs. buy, a quick answer now vs. a reusable model later

  • You turn analysis into decisions. You can explain a finding to a non-technical leader in a few sentences and tell them what to do about it

  • You communicate clearly, write clean, tested code, and lead through technical decisions whether or not you're managing people yet

  • You have very high agency. You don't wait to be told which problem to work on; you go and find the ones that matter

Nice to have

  • You've been an early or founding data hire at a fast-growing fintech

  • Experience with real money data at a fintech: payments, cards, ledgers, settlement, chargebacks or FX. You know the ways financial data goes wrong

  • Hands-on fraud, risk or financial-crime analytics

  • Familiarity with stablecoins and on-chain data, including how blockchain transactions map to accounts, balances and ledgers

  • Experience hiring and growing a data team

  • Machine learning in production for fraud, risk or personalisation

What's in it for you

  • Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

  • A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

  • Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

  • Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

  • All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

  • Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

About us

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

What you’ll do

  • Design and deliver production-grade AI agents: You'll build and ship highly performant, reliable, and intuitive AI agents that are central, mission-critical and drive revenue directly to Sierra's growth. These aren't prototypes—they are powerful, scalable systems running in production environments across industries like finance, healthcare, and commerce.

  • Drive the Agent Development Life Cycle (ADLC): You'll have complete ownership and autonomy from initial pilot through deployment and continuous iteration. You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

  • Partner with large enterprises and cutting-edge startups: You’ll work directly with leaders at some of the world’s largest enterprises to understand their most pressing business challenges, and build AI agents that transform how they operate at scale. You'll also partner with the most cutting-edge startups in Silicon Valley, embedding AI agents across their entire business stack to drive innovation and efficiency.

  • Build the future of the platform: Your direct work with customers will guide the evolution of Sierra's core platform. You'll surface unmet needs, prototype new tools and features, and collaborate with research, product, and platform to shape the future of AI agent development and Sierra's product.

Example projects

These are some examples of projects that engineers on our team have worked on recently:

  • Design and build AI agents for large telecommunications and media companies that consistently outperform human agents in managing subscription churn

  • Develop and refine AI agents capable of navigating complex customer interactions, like troubleshooting a broken device and personalizing product recommendations

  • Create generalizable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog!

  • Facilitate design partnerships for new product initiatives, such as new agent architectures, self-service capabilities, and generative agent development

  • Experiment with the latest voice models and figure out how to integrate them at scale to enterprise-grade customers

What you'll bring

  • Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems

  • Strong technical problem-solving skills, especially in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

  • A builder and tinkerer’s mindset with high agency - you find creative ways to overcome obstacles and ship

  • Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems

  • Excellent communication skills - clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences

Even better...

  • Experience building or deploying AI/LLM systems in production

  • Have been a founder or founding engineer - you know what it means to balance craft, ownership, and speed

  • Prior experience with React, TypeScript, and/or Go

  • Previous roles where you interfaced with customers or led technical projects with external stakeholders

We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

  • Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

  • Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

As the Art Director you will set the visual standard for the company's materials and produce them: product and capability collateral, presentations, exhibition and event graphics, digital and social assets, and the images that explain the systems themselves.

This is a role for someone who both directs and who is hands on. It spans print, digital, environmental and presentation design rather than specialising in one, and it serves the whole company - sales, government relations, recruitment and the executive team, not marketing alone.

It is also where visual consistency is held. External agencies, photographers, 3D artists and film-makers deliver into the UFORCE brand; the Art Director sets what they work to and judges what comes back. The standard is that everything the company puts in front of a customer reads as though it came from one place.

What you will do

  • Design the materials the company sells and speaks with: capability collateral, specification sheets, presentations, launch assets, digital and social graphics.

  • Help evolve the UFORCE visual system - typography, colour, layout, iconography and the treatment of platform imagery - and keep it documented well enough that others can work to it.

  • Turn technical material - system architectures, concepts of operation, platform diagrams - into images a non-specialist can understand.

  • Design exhibition and event graphics, from stand panels to printed handouts.

  • Art-direct photography, film and 3D work, on location and in review, so that commissioned material comes back usable and on-brand.

  • Active use of AI tools in how work is run and delivered, and an appetite to commission or build workflows that do not yet exist rather than wait for them.

  • Direct localisation of work across the company's markets.

  • Apply the company's security and export-control requirements to visual material, and route imagery of platforms, facilities and personnel for clearance before release.

Required Skills

  • Substantial experience as a Graphic designer or art director, in-house or in an agency, with a portfolio showing both range and finished craft across print, digital and environmental work.

  • Command of typography, hierarchy and composition, and a body of work that holds to a consistent system rather than a collection of one-off styles.

  • The ability to art-direct others - photographers, film-makers, illustrators, 3D artists - from written brief through review to delivery.

  • Deep fluency in Figma, the company's primary design environment: components, variants and shared libraries, not frames alone. Working knowledge of InDesign and Illustrator for print and large-format work.

  • Willingness to master Google Slides. Presentations are a primary sales instrument.

  • Experience making complex or technical subject matter legible, in any field - engineering, science, medicine, infrastructure or defence.

  • Eligibility to gain UK security clearance

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing for defence, dual-use or engineering-led products

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

As the Video Producer & Editor, you will be the point between raw footage and published work. The output goes onto company channels, into the hands of sales and government relations, and in front of closed-door audiences—including material that cannot leave the building.

Video is the clearest evidence of what UFORCE does to those outside the military. The systems are real, they are in use, and footage of them shows our customers what no render or animation can. In a market full of future-tense capability claims, that is the differentiator, and this role is what converts it into content people actually see.

This is not an assembly role. You are expected to shape and direct content as well as cut it: to decide what is worth capturing, what the film is, and what to leave out. The register is real and observed rather than advertised. The standard is publishable as it leaves the timeline.

It is a mid-level role with unusual freedom. There is no post-production team and no producer. The work is daily, the subject matter is serious, and there is room for someone who wants to build their craft on material most editors never get near.

 

What you will do

  • Cut and finish film for company channels, social platforms, sales and government relations, and internal and closed-door audiences.

  • Shape content from the outset: propose ideas, write shot lists and capture briefs, and direct or shoot capture where needed.

  • Deliver distinct cuts for distinct audiences rather than reformatting one film for all of them.

  • Finish to a publishable standard—grade, sound, captioning, titling and versioning.

  • Own the footage library: cataloguing, archive structure, backup and version control.

  • Hold the UFORCE film language and keep output consistent, including work delivered by external film-makers.

  • Travel to facilities, ranges, events and deployments, sometimes at short notice, and film in industrial and field conditions.

  • Utilise approved AI tools to optimize your workflow, strictly adhering to data security guidelines and ensuring no sensitive material leaves secure networks.

  • Apply the company's security and export-control requirements to footage, and route material showing platforms, facilities and personnel for clearance before release.

 

Required Skills

  • Around three to six years of professional editing experience, with a showreel of published work rather than showpieces.

  • Command of pacing, structure and sound, and the ability to explain the decisions behind a cut—particularly what was removed.

  • Experience in a factual, documentary, news or event register, not branded content alone.

  • Evidence of consistent output at pace, self-managed: media handling, versioning and deadlines without a producer.

  • A piece taken from idea and shot list through to final cut.

  • Fluency in a professional NLE—Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut—with working knowledge of After Effects or equivalent for basic motion work.

  • Sound judgement with confidential, embargoed or otherwise restricted material.

  • A point of view on what good looks like, and the willingness to argue for it.

  • Right to work in the UK and eligibility to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC level).

 

Nice to Have

  • Camera operation to a publishable standard, including commercial drone operation (with CAA certification).

  • Motion graphics and titling beyond basics.

  • Stills photography.

  • Experience cutting technical or engineering subject matter.

  • Experience in defence, dual-use or uncrewed systems, whether in industry or in service.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

Are You?

raw.description:
🚀 About WRITER

WRITER is where the world's leading enterprises orchestrate AI-powered work. Our vision is to expand human capacity through super-intelligence. And we're proving it's possible – through powerful, trustworthy AI that unites IT and business teams together to unlock enterprise-wide transformation. With WRITER's end-to-end platform, hundreds of companies like Mars, Marriott, Uber, and Vanguard are building and deploying AI agents that are grounded in their company's data and fueled by WRITER's enterprise-grade LLMs. Valued at $1.9B and backed by industry-leading investors including Premji Invest, Radical Ventures, and ICONIQ Growth, WRITER is rapidly cementing its position as the leader in enterprise generative AI.

Founded in 2020 with office hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Austin, Chicago, and London, our team thinks big and moves fast, and we're looking for smart, hardworking builders and scalers to join us on our journey to create a better future of work with AI.

📐 About the role

Join WRITER's sales team as a strategic account executive and help shape the future of work. You'll empower global enterprises (8,000+ employees) to transform their operations through our cutting-edge AI agent platform, enabling organizations to deploy AI at scale and unlock unprecedented productivity. This isn't just about hitting quota – it's about becoming a trusted advisor to some of the world's most influential companies as they navigate their AI transformation journey.

This role is perfect for high performers who thrive in fast-paced, intellectually stimulating environments where you have the autonomy to drive results and build lasting relationships with both clients and teammates. If you're energized by meaningful work, the opportunity to make a real impact, and the challenge of selling category-defining technology, we want to hear from you. You'll be selling solutions that fundamentally change how enterprises operate, working with executive buyers who are making multi-million dollar, multi-year commitments to AI transformation.

This is a hybrid role based out of our London hub. You'll be reporting to our regional vice president.

🦸🏻‍♀️ What you need

  • 7-10+ years of quota-carrying strategic SaaS sales experience with a proven track record of meeting or exceeding annual quotas in complex, value-based sales motions targeting Fortune 500 and Global 2000 financial services accounts

  • Deep understanding of the UK and European financial services landscape — banking, asset management, insurance, and fintech — including its regulatory environment, buying cycles, and communication standards

  • Demonstrated expertise in managing sophisticated enterprise sales cycles with multiple stakeholders, navigating procurement and security processes, and orchestrating cross-functional resources to drive deals through technical evaluations and executive approvals

  • Executive presence and communication skills that allow you to credibly engage with C-suite buyers (CIOs, CDOs, CTOs, COOs), translate complex technical concepts into business value, and build authentic relationships based on trust and strategic insight

  • Strong consultative selling skills with the ability to conduct discovery that uncovers underlying business challenges, connects AI capabilities to measurable outcomes, and creates urgency around transformation initiatives in regulated industries

  • Experience in outbound prospecting, account mapping, and territory planning, with a hunter mentality that drives you to consistently create new opportunities rather than waiting for inbound leads

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a bias for ownership — you thrive in fast-paced environments where you're expected to figure things out, make decisions with incomplete information, and drive your own success with minimal oversight

  • Deep alignment with WRITER's values: you naturally Connect across functions and build collaborative relationships, you Challenge the status quo and aren't afraid to have difficult conversations, and you Own your outcomes with accountability and a commitment to long-term impact

⭐️ Is this you?

  • You've sold into financial services institutions and understand what it takes to navigate complex, regulated buying environments — from security and compliance reviews to board-level approvals

  • You're a closer who has consistently carried and exceeded seven-figure quotas, and you can point to deals where you created the opportunity from scratch rather than working an inbound lead

  • You think like a consultant but sell like a hunter — your discovery uncovers pain buyers didn't know they had, and your storytelling connects AI to outcomes that matter to a CIO and a CFO alike

  • You understand the UK FS market specifically — the players, the regulators, the buying rhythms — and you have or can build a network that opens doors

  • You're comfortable in the boardroom and the back office — equally credible presenting an AI transformation vision to an exec team and working through the technical and procurement details with the people who sign off

  • You move fast, own your number, and don't wait to be told what to do next

Preferred skills

  • Existing network and relationships within UK or European financial services institutions

  • Background in management consulting, particularly with FS clients

  • Experience selling AI, data, or enterprise platform deals into regulated industries

  • Familiarity with the compliance, security, and governance requirements that shape FS buying decisions

  • Experience supporting or leading large-scale rollouts or change management programs

  • Strong storytelling and presentation skills for executive audiences

🍩 Benefits & perks (UK full-time employees):

  • Generous PTO, plus company holidays

  • Comprehensive medical and dental insurance

  • Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks)

  • Fertility and family planning support

  • Early-detection cancer testing through Galleri

  • Competitive pension scheme and company contribution

  • Annual work-life stipends for:

    • Wellness stipend for gym, massage/chiropractor, personal training, etc.

    • Learning and development stipend

  • Company-wide off-sites and team off-sites

  • Competitive compensation and company stock options
